label: unstable dryad
attackSummary: left claw(8p/2s); right claw(8p/2s); Bite(9p/2s); head(4p/2s)
description: A dangerous dryad caste that will explode with acid when dead. They can be commanded to explode... for the good of the tree.\n\nIn general, dryads are mammal-like creatures that have a symbiotic relationship with the Gauranlen tree. They reproduce together with their tree, which contains a hidden dryad queen. Dryads can morph into various specialized castes.

label: unshackled dryad
attackSummary: left claw(8p/2s); right claw(8p/2s); Bite(9p/2s); head(4p/2s)
description: Dryads are small mammalian creatures that have a symbiotic relationship with the Gauranlen tree.\n\nThis particular dryad seems to be unshackled, and it will not leave the region if no Gauranlen trees are around.

label: bulbfreak
attackSummary: tentacle(7p/2s); tentacle(7p/2s); tentacle(7p/2s); tentacle(7p/2s); tentacle(7p/2s); head(3p/2s)
description: A horrid oozing amalgamation of many smaller fleshbeasts, all controlled by a linked nervous system. It has two large claws which it uses to tear through its victims. Bulbfreaks are often smelled before they are seen, giving off an overwhelming odor of rancid meat. They are relatively slow and easy to kill, but once they die, they explode into a horde of smaller fleshbeasts.

label: chimera
attackSummary: left claw(17p/2s); right claw(17p/2s); Bite(23.6p/2.6s); head(11p/2s)
description: A huge creature that resembles a disfigured combination of a bear and other animals. It is vicious without limit.\n\nIt's not known if this is a combination of natural animals or a poor imitation of animal life created by an insane machine mind.

label: human
attackSummary: left fist(8.2p/2s); right fist(8.2p/2s); teeth(8.2p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: A baseline human, mostly unmodified by gene engineering and mostly unchanged by evolutionary pressures on non-Earth planets.

label: devourer
description: A massive monster with a gaping toothed maw and a stubby, snake-like body. The devourer can leap several times its body length to swallow a person whole. Powerful stomach acids rapidly digest the still-living victim. The remains are regurgitated soon after.

label: dreadmeld
description: A gargantuan amalgamation of dozens of smaller fleshbeasts linked together by a loosely shared central nervous system. It uses its massive claws to dig tunnels through solid rock. Fleshbeast dreadmelds are rarely seen above ground, instead sheltering in caverns built from living flesh. They share a psychic connection with the flesh used to create their burrow.

label: fingerspike
description: A fleshy dog-sized creature with a single spiked limb. Despite their short legs, fingerspikes can move remarkably fast.

label: fleshmass nucleus
description: The archotech core of a fleshmass heart. It is a chaotic lattice of fluid-smeared metal. Solid chunks of jagged metal appear here and there, packed with archotechnology. The whole structure slowly twists and bends under its own power.\n\nIt constantly grows meat on its surface, which occasionally erupts violently. If too much meat builds up, it will regrow into a fleshmass heart.

label: gorehulk
attackSummary: left flesh club(3p/1.5s); right flesh club(3p/1.5s); head(3p/2s)
description:
A monstrous creature that resembles a massive, painfully swollen human with randomly reconfigured body parts. Near its top is a stretched face that watches its victim with dead eyes.

Hundreds of sharp keratin spines protrude from the gorehulk's skin. It can launch these spines to spear its victims at a distance. However, its awkward fleshy body is less effective at causing harm up close.

It'

label: metalhorror
description:
A horrific shifting mass of metal filaments, blades, and instruments. This metal is maintained and regenerated by a circulating dark fluid.

While dormant, fluid metalhorrors are hidden in a host body. They use their host to infect others, creating more metalhorrors. If detected or endangered, the metalhorror will form a jagged exoskeleton and cut its way out of the host's flesh.

An emerged m

label: nociosphere
description: A dark metallic sphere covered with curved and jagged grooves. The sphere emanates sensations of pain. It hurts to be near it.\n\nThe sphere thrums with a mysterious energy. It appears to be increasing in activity. It's not clear what will happen when it reaches its full capacity. However, if you capture it, you can decrease its activity by suppressing it.

label: noctol
attackSummary: left claw(12.3p/1.25s); right claw(12.3p/1.25s); Bite(15p/2s); head(9p/2s)
description: A large, chittering creature covered with an oily black carapace and armed with claws formed from bioferrite. While it is deadly in the dark, exposure to light irritates its eyes and flesh, slowing it down considerably.

label: revenant
description: A spindly figure of desiccated skin stretched over an impossibly tall humanoid frame. The revenant's name comes from its pattern of returning to hypnotize new people each night.\n\nOutlander folklore describes an invisible spectre that captures the minds of sinners, placing them in a living hell. In the story, the victims can only be returned to life by hunting the creature as it sleeps and killin

label: sightstealer
description: Emaciated and misshapen humanoids. Their arms end in sharp, curled claws formed from bioferrite. Sightstealers are fragile, but use psychic influence to render themselves invisible until they get close to their victims. They are known to emit haunting screams as they gather on their terrible hunts.

label: toughspike
description: A fleshy man-sized creature with two spiked limbs and an armored carapace. Toughspikes throw hardened keratin spikes to take down victims from a distance.\n\nToughspike corpses will dissolve into puddles of liquefied flesh if they're not butchered quickly.

label: trispike
attackSummary: left spike(7p/2s); right spike(7p/2s); top spike(7p/2s); head(3p/2s)
description: A man-sized amalgamation of several smaller fleshbeasts. Each of the creature's limbs is capable of surviving independently. On death, trispikes may split into separate fingerspikes as each limb rips free and attacks.

label: alligator man
attackSummary: left fist(8.2p/2s); right fist(8.2p/2s); teeth(18.2p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: A large person with the head of an alligator.

label: armadillo
attackSummary: left claw(8p/2s); right claw(8p/2s); Bite(10p/2.6s); head(5p/2s)
description: A desert mammal with a leathery armour shell. The armadillo is well-adapted for defense against larger predators.

label: bardelot
attackSummary: left claw(4p/2s); right claw(4p/2s); Bite(6p/2.6s); head(3p/2s)
description: A large, migratory, tundra-dwelling predator rat from the Northern Hemisphere tundra. It is capable of producing litters with genetic input from many mates.

label: black bear
attackSummary: left claw(17p/2s); right claw(17p/2s); Bite(23.6p/2.6s); head(11p/2s)
description: Black bears are extremely adaptable and show a great variation in habitat types, though they are primarily found in forested areas with thick ground vegetation and an abundance of fruits, nuts, and vegetation. In the northern areas, they can be found in the tundra, and they will sometimes forage in fields or meadows.

label: black bear man
attackSummary: left fist(8.2p/2s); right fist(8.2p/2s); Bite(23.6p/2.6s); head(11p/2s)
description: A large person with the head of a black bear

label: giantala
description: A large ground sloth-like marsupial that lives in the undergrowth of the tropical forests. Its giant tail acts as an extra leg to help it stand upright.

label: gigantelope
description: An enormous creature with short legs. These giant herbivores have long abandoned the antelopes running gait and taken on a plodding existence.

label: jerbal
description: A large kangaroo-like gerbil adapted to desert environments. It uses its tail to store fat. It can go for long periods without eating when food is unavailable.

label: mandrill
attackSummary: left fist(10p/1.3s); right fist(10p/1.3s); Bite(4p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: Mandrills are colorful, large monkeys of the old world. Large groups of them live in the tropical rainforests.

label: mandrill man
attackSummary: left fist(8.2p/2s); right fist(8.2p/2s); Bite(4p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: A blue-rumped person with the head of a mandrill.

label: megasquid
description: The megasquid is a large omnivorous terasquid. Heavier than an elephant and almost as tall, a megasquid lumbers through the forest, moving at speeds similar to a human's walking pace.

label: neanderthal
attackSummary: left fist(10p/2s); right fist(10p/2s); teeth(8.2p/2s); head(6p/2s)
description: Hunanity's closest relative. Neanderthals communicate using primitive vocalizations without understanding actual language. They are apex predators, capable of bringing down a wide range of prey.

label: penguin
description: An aquatic, flightless bird native to the coldest climates. Known for their cuteness. They are friendly to humans.

label: rabbuck
attackSummary: left hoof(8p/2s); right hoof(8p/2s); Bite(10p/2s); head(13p/2.6s)
description: Heavily built with rolls of insulating fat, the rabbuck is found in the far north of the continent, in the region of the tundra and coniferous forests.

label: toraton
description: Due to its sheer size, an adult toraton has no predators and no longer has any need for a shell. Small sections of the ancestoral shell do remain, however, forming an external support for the creature's muscles, which its feeble ribs and vertebrae alone cannot carry.

label: worm
description: A large worm. Its digestive system runs through the length of its body. Worms reproduce quickly.

label: yippa
attackSummary: left hoof(7.3p/2s); right hoof(7.3p/2s); Bite(8p/2s); head(7p/2s)
description: A long necked lama-like herbivore. Native to tropical climates. The upper layers of vegetation are exploited by the yippa.

label: zarander
description: The zarander is a large elephant-like suine. Despite its large trunk, it has little sense of smell. It relies on keen hearing to detect predators.

label: zebra
attackSummary: head(10p/2.9s); left hoof(7p/2s); right hoof(7p/2s); Bite(5p/2s)
description: A black and white striped herbivore. They are stubborn and have never been truely domesticated.

label: queen
description: The insect queen is the mother of the brood. She usually stays secluded deep in the hive. She is extremely dangerous and the colony will defend her at all cost.

label: race-that-the-author-forgot-to-give-a-name
attackSummary: left fist(8.2p/2s); right fist(8.2p/2s); teeth(8.2p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: A race with a neglected description.

label: mech
attackSummary: left fist(8.2p/2s); right fist(8.2p/2s); teeth(8.2p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: This is a creature largely composed of highly ruggedized machinery.

label: centauroid
attackSummary: left fist(8.2p/2s); right fist(8.2p/2s); teeth(8.2p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: The subject is quadrupedeal with a humanoid torso.

label: Four Armed Human
attackSummary: left fist(8.2p/2s); right fist(8.2p/2s); teeth(8.2p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: A humanlike being with a great forearms, no, wait FOUR great arms.

label: tailed humanoid
attackSummary: left fist(8.2p/2s); right fist(8.2p/2s); teeth(8.2p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: The inclusion of a tail statistically improves the sense of balance of the specimen uwu.

label: winged humanoid
attackSummary: left fist(8.2p/2s); right fist(8.2p/2s); teeth(8.2p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: Scientists think that humans should not be able to fly.

label: disembodied head
description: I was told by the customer to engineer them with as big a head as possible. I did exactly what I was told. (Project: "Make anime real", attempt 412)

label: six-armed snake-person
attackSummary: left fist(8.2p/2s); right fist(8.2p/2s); teeth(8.2p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: A humanlike being with a six arms and a snake tail instead of legs.

label: snake-person
attackSummary: left fist(8.2p/2s); right fist(8.2p/2s); teeth(8.2p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: A humanlike being with a snake tail instead of legs.

label: Six Armed Human
attackSummary: left fist(8.2p/2s); right fist(8.2p/2s); teeth(8.2p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: A humanlike being with an excessively large number of arms.

label: spider-person
attackSummary: left fist(8.2p/2s); right fist(8.2p/2s); teeth(8.2p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: A humanlike being with a spider-like abdomen.

label: glutton
attackSummary: left fist(8.2p/2s); right fist(8.2p/2s); teeth(8.2p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: At a distance they could be mistaken for being human...

label: insect-like humanoid
attackSummary: left fist(8.2p/2s); right fist(8.2p/2s); teeth(8.2p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: A humanlike being with four arms, four eyes, and four times the chance of frightening outlanders.

label: aaroxis dendoria
description: Uniquely engineered for life in an underground environment, this moth has been altered to produce silk even in adulthood, at the cost of remaining wingless.

label: cinnabar caterpillar
description: A unique species of moth larva with a spiraling body pattern rather than the normal segmented. It is thought to be a genetic anomaly from its engineered creation. The crimson-colored silk it produces is luxuriously soft.

label: aaroxis dendoria pupa
description: Even in their pupal stage, their red abdomen can be seen as they metamorphose. They are almost entirely immobile in this stage.

label: acid slug
description: Originally designed for combat, the acid slug is one of the most dangerous predators in the earthen depths due to its highly acidic slime and flesh. The bodies of its prey are melted down to the bone within its gelatinous flesh.

label: basilisk
attackSummary: left claw(8p/2s); right claw(8p/2s); Bite(10p/2.6s); head(5p/2s)
description: With eyes that enrapture its prey should they gaze into them, the six-legged basilisk is both designed and named after its mythological predecessor.

label: batbird
description: An engineered hybrid of mammal and avian, the batbird lives in shallow caves below the desert sands. It feeds on small prey and gives birth to live young.

label: bearded yak
attackSummary: left hoof(10p/2s); right hoof(10p/2s); Bite(10p/2s); head(13p/2.6s)
description: A large member of the yak family, well-adapted to life in climates of bitter cold. Unfortunately for some, they cannot be sheared for their fur.

label: bloodrop larvae
description: The larval form of the bloodrop moth. It gains nutrients for growth by feeding on the blood of any large creature. A small group of them can drain even an elephant to death in minutes.

label: bloodrop moth
description: The adult form of this species. It flies near silently through cave systems in search of blood it can drain from prey using its razor sharp proboscis. Much like bats, they live in large groups.\n\nEven a small group of them can drain a large animal to death in mere minutes.

label: bloodrop pupa
description: The pupal stage of the bloodrop moth. It uses the nutrients it gained from blood as a larvae to survive, which also causes its deep red color. While quite vulnerable in this life stage, they are not entirely defenseless, as their pupa exterior is quite hardened.

label: bovine beetle
description: A large beetle originally from Caveworlds, this bug is often kept in farms for its production of a milk-like substance and flakes of chitin.

label: bovine grub
description: A large grub originally from Caveworlds, this bug is often kept in farms for the milk-like substance it produces as an adult. It is the larval form of the bovine beetle.

label: bovine pupa
description: A large beetle, commonly found in dark, damp places. Milkable.\n\nA large beetle originally from Caveworlds, this bug is often kept in farms for its production of a milk-like substance.

label: brown bat
description: It's a flappy herbivorous mammal. These bats flit around within the dark, using their sense of echolocation to locate prey, typically small insects or mammals.

label: cactus crab
description: A smaller relative of the crystal crab, adapted to desert-like underground environments. They grow cacti on their shell for camoflauge and defense. From birth, they find a rock and settle into it as their shell.

label: cave cricket
description: While often considered a pest to cave-dwellers, some have domesticated these meaty crickets for their own use as disgusting but hearty food. They grow fast and lay a multitude of eggs in mere days.

label: cave lemming
description: This big, solitary herbivore can swiftly hop away from danger.

label: cave spider
description: Huge and horrifying, these spiders are one of the most dangerous predators in the UnderRim. They are fiercely territorial and intelligent, with a tendency to lay claim to commonly traveled tunnels for easy prey, including humanoids. Their powerful bite injects potent venom into their victims.

label: chem snail
description: Engineered much like the surface-dwelling Boomalope, this snail produces volatile chemicals within its shell. Even the strongest predators of the caverns have learned to avoid it, as the chemsnail explodes upon death. Its slime can be carefully harvested for chemfuel.

label: crested dragon
attackSummary: left claw(9p/2s); right claw(9p/2s); Blunt(12p/2.6s); head(8p/2s)
description: Much like the prehistoric Parasaur, this lizard has a crest. The purpose is largely for display, but also allows them to make cute squeaky noises.

label: crystalback beetle
description: A small and quick beetle adapted to the crystal-laden caverns. It secretes a sticky goo from its mouth to glue shards of crystal to its shell for defense and camouflage.

label: crystalback grub
description: Small and relatively slow, this chubby grub hides among crystals to avoid predators. Its main defense is spewing sticky goo at their eyes.

label: crystalback pupa
description: The pupal form of the crystalback beetle. Its body has largely liquified as it metamorphoses within.

label: crystal crab
description: A large and powerful relative of the decorator crab, cavern crystals grow from the minerals on this crab's rocky shell. Despite its strong exoskeleton, the crystal crab hauls around this heavy shell, the reason for which is unknown. They are not known to breed in captivity.

label: crystal fairy mole
attackSummary: left claw(7.5p/2s); right claw(7.5p/2s); Bite(10p/2.6s); head(6p/2s)
description: Crystal plating covers the back of this mole species, offering protection from predators and hunters.

label: crystal mimic mantis
attackSummary: mandibles(9p/2s); left scythe(11p/2s); right scythe(11p/2s); head(5p/3s)
description: A native to the crystal caverns, this mantis is nearly the size of a person. It uses its crystal-like carapace as camouflage while hunting prey.

label: crystalope
attackSummary: head(7p/2s); left hoof(9p/2s); right hoof(9p/2s); Bite(10p/2s)
description: Though weak and fragile, the crystalope was engineered to grow large crystals on its back. Other animals have learned to avoid it because of the huge explosion it produces upon death. Its crystal can be harvested.

label: dark axolotl
attackSummary: left claw(7p/2.0s); right claw(7p/2.0s); jaw(9p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: A large yet peaceful inhabitant of the shallow caves. Hunts only small animals. A good pet, though weak in combat.

label: diggerpede
description: The predatory diggerpede is found below the desert surface, burrowing in the sand and soil faster than most can run. It hunts anything it can lay its mandibles on when it hungers.\n\nDespite being similar to other arthropods, it gives live birth rather than lay eggs.

label: facet moth
description: A large moth with wings that glimmer like the facets of crystal. It flits about in dark caverns and is often captured and kept as a pet for its beauty. The females are capable of producing multiple batches of fertilized eggs from one mating period.

label: crystalline caterpillar
description: The larval form of the facet moth. To deter predators, its body appears spiky and hard through a form of natural mimicry.

label: facet pupa
description: The pupal form of the facet moth. While immobile, its hard shell protects it from most predators.

label: fire salamander
attackSummary: left claw(9p/2s); right claw(9p/2s); Blunt(12p/2.6s); head(8p/2s)
description: Though commonly called a salamander, it is more closely related to reptiles than amphibians. Its luminous skin is reminiscent of hot lava. Normally this would deter its natural predators if it weren't for their poor vision.

label: fleece spider
description: Small and fluffy, these spiders have become a popular pet amongst the cavern-dwelling populace. It can be easily fed from whatever food falls onto the ground.

label: foundry beetle
description: While herbivorous, this beetle is no easy prey. It uses its massive mandibles to crush both rival mates and anything that tries to hunt it. These beetles are often bred as war bugs by the more vicious cave dwellers.

label: foundry grub
description: A small and soft grub with inflammable chitin. Unfortunately this does not last once the grub is dead.

label: foundry pupa
description: The pupal form of the foundry beetle. Its body has largely liquified as it metamorphoses within. It is completely inflammable in nature.

label: freezer frog
description: This small, herbivorous frog has special chemicals in its blood that allow it to survive in sub-zero temperatures. Due to the scarcity of liquid water, their young hatch into miniature adults rather than tadpoles.

label: frostweaver
description: Engineered for the freezing cold tunnels and caverns found in areas that never see a summer, the fuzz that grows on these beastly spiders forms into icy peaks. These spiders are antisocial and are known to attack when enraged.

label: fungal ferret
attackSummary: left claw(7p/2s); right claw(7p/2s); Bite(8p/2s); head(3p/2s)
description: The fungus growing on the back of this small mammal has formed a mutual bond with its host, living primarily within and on its fur.

label: fungal mimic mantis
attackSummary: mandibles(9p/2s); left scythe(7p/2s); right scythe(7p/2s); head(5p/3s)
description: A native to the fungal forest caverns, this mantis is larger than a person. It uses its fungus-covered carapace as camouflage while hunting. Unlike other mantises, they rely on their attacks injecting anesthetic and poisonous chemicals into prey.

label: fungal weevil
description: Unlike normal fungal infestations within insects, this infestation has somehow grown into a healthy symbiosis. The insect's movements help to spread the fungal spores while its body provides the fungus a home. In return, the fungus helps its host hide within the fungal growths of the biome.

label: gembug
description: Commonly found in crystal caverns, the gembug is a smaller relative of the pillbug known for its gem-like exoskeleton.

label: giant slug
description: A huge slug, roughly the size of a pig. It is often used as a meat source for underground colonies.

label: giant snail
description: A gigantic herd snail used as a pack animal by many cavern-dwelling societies. Its ability to adhere to and climb virtually any surface makes it invaluable for traders or travelers underground.

label: glarral penguin
description: Large-beaked penguins that use their beaks to carve out dens and dig for food in hollowed out glaciers and frozen wastes.

label: bioluminescent bat
description: Feasting on the bioluminescent plants and fungi within the caverns has caused this bat to adapt a similar trait.

label: glowslug
description: This bioluminescent slug is easily spotted in any dark environment, both by its own species and by predators. It is a wonder how they have survived this long, let alone to such a large size.

label: goeto tadpole
description: The larval form of the goeto toad. It survives in the often murky waters in caverns, feeding off any biological detritus it can.

label: goeto toad
attackSummary: left claw(2p/2s); right claw(2p/2s); Bite(3p/2s); head(1p/2s)
description: The goeto toad is another attempt at creating a meat and egg source for mining exportation centers and underground colonies. The project rapidly got out of hand, and the specimens quickly adapted to the caves which became its new 'natural' habitat.

label: hoarfrost mastodon
attackSummary: tusk(25p/2.6s); left foot(16.9p/2s); right foot(16.9p/2s); head(14p/2s)
description: Hoarfrost mastodon has a long trunk they use to manipulate objects, and sharp curved tusks they use to gore and smash attackers. A dead mastodon's valuable tusks can be recovered by butchering it.\n\nIntelligent creatures with complex social relationships, mastodons can be trained to carry out the most complex of tasks. They live a long time, and are known to remember events and relationships from

label: hungering hydra
description: With three heads and just as many stomachs, this massive ravenous beast almost constantly scours cave systems for food. They are protected by strong natural armor and their razor sharp teeth, with any injuries they do sustain healing rapidly.

label: imperial toad
attackSummary: left claw(2p/2s); right claw(2p/2s); Bite(3p/2s); head(1p/2s)
description: The imperial toad is native to the cave systems below deserts on the Rim. It tends to be preyed upon quite easily but many cave dwellers have taken a shine to it as a pet due to its regal posture.

label: jellypot
description: Named the jellypot for its ability to produce insect jelly in its large thoracic sac, this rare animal is almost exclusively found near insectoid hives. Despite being farmed much like ants do with aphids, it does not seem capable of breeding in captivity.

label: jewel beetle
description: A small yet pretty beetle native to the desert shallows. Its brightly colored shell makes it valuable for its looks.

label: jewel grub
description: Small and relatively ugly, this little grub hides among sand and rocks to avoid potential predators. It lacks any proper defenses.

label: jewel pupa
description: The pupal form of the jewel beetle. Its body has largely liquified as it metamorphoses within.

label: mace drake
attackSummary: left wing(4p/6s); right wing(4p/6s); rear left foot(4p/6s); rear right foot(4p/6s); Bite(10p/2s); head(15p/2.5s); tail-club(20p/2s)
description: Despite their fierce draconic appearance, the mace drake is actually a fairly passive herbivore. However, it willingly uses its clubbed tail as a weapon if harassed.

label: maguana
attackSummary: left claw(8p/2s); right claw(8p/2s); Bite(10p/2.6s); head(5p/2s)
description: The patterning on the skin of this relative of the surface iguana resembles both cooled and hot magma, seemingly to blend in with the volatile environment within the cavern systems. They are naturally immune to fire due to the special composition of their flesh.

label: megabat
description: This massive species of bat has become largely flightless, instead walking on its wings. It has learned to use its echolocation as a weapon to disorient prey.

label: megapleura
description: A relative of the trilobite beetle, the megapleura has grown to massive proportions while living deep within the Rim's crust. While odd in appearance, it is largely harmless.

label: metallosnail
description: Adapted or engineered to survive the considerable heat and volatility near the molten layer, the metallosnail has gained the ability to grow metal for its shell. It also produces thin plates of metal to protect its softer bits.

label: mole
attackSummary: left claw(8p/1.5s); right claw(8p/1.5s); Bite(8p/2s); head(7p/2s)
description: The mole is usually found within shallower caverns, digging through terrain faster than it otherwise walks.

label: Molebear
attackSummary: left claw(18p/2s); right claw(18p/2s); Bite(20.0p/2.6s); head(12p/2s)
description: Created from a genetic mix of mole and bear, it was released into the wild and has found a home within caverns near the surface. It comes and goes as it pleases.

label: moss beetle
description: A large beetle, commonly found in dark, damp places.\n\nIt feeds off low underbrush in fungal forests and while not the best source of meat, it works when little else is available.

label: moss grub
description: A large beetle commonly found in dark, damp places, it feeds off low underbrush in caverns. While not the best source of meat, it works when little else is available.

label: moss pupa
description: A large beetle, commonly found in dark, damp places.\n\nIt feeds off low underbrush in fungal forests and while not the best source of meat, it works when little else is available.

label: mossy fennec
attackSummary: left claw(8p/2s); right claw(8p/2s); Bite(9p/2s); head(4p/2s)
description: This fox species has formed a unique mutual bond with a type of symbiotic moss, providing the moss with motility and access to water and nutrients. In return, the moss provides energy via contact with the fox's skin.

label: pillbug
description: The large isopod inhabits the bottom of the cavern food chain. It feeds on virtually any filth it finds, keeping the tunnels and catacombs clean.

label: pod worm
description: Though large and intimidating, the appearance of this strange insectoid-like creature does not match with its otherwise passive nature. While it typically lives in insectoid hives as a part of the glow pod producing caste, it occasionally wanders off or gets captured and sold by humanoids.

label: rimebeak
description: As big and tough as a warg, this avian creature hosts a blade-sharp beak. Its two sets of eyes allow it to expertly see in near-absolute darkness.

label: royal rhino beetle
description: A gigantic type of rare beetle that is revered by certain underground cultures for its rarity and power. While its royal purple chitin is beautiful, it is also extremely durable. The extremely sharp horn gracing their head fetches a high price. While normally gentle by nature, it is extremely dangerous when enraged.

label: royal rhino grub
description: A gigantic larva of the royal rhino beetle. It is much weaker than its adult form, often remaining reclusive until fully grown.

label: royal rhino pupa
description: A vary large and highly durable pupa. While immobile, its shell protects it from most harm.

label: sand leaper
description: A desert rodent related to the common surface rat. While its main defense is mostly being small and quick, it has some natural chitinous armor as well.

label: sandpillar
description: Similarly to some species of salamander, this colossal caterpillar stays in its juvenile state for life but remains able to reproduce despite this.

label: shatterjaw beetle
description: One of the most dangerous inhabitants of the crystal caves, the shatterjaw hunt with their large mandibles, crushing and cutting prey to pieces before feeding.

label: shatterjaw grub
description: While its adult form can bite a man in half, this weak, squishy grub is incapable of such a task.

label: shatterjaw pupa
description: The pupal form of the shatterjaw beetle. Its body has largely liquified as it metamorphoses within. It has perhaps the most durable exterior out of all known pupae.

label: shimmershell snail
description: Similar to the other gigantic snail species found underground and on Caveworlds, this species has been modified to bioluminesce.

label: silver sheep
attackSummary: head(14p/2.9s); left hoof(6p/2s); right hoof(6p/2s); Bite(8p/2s)
description: Silver sheep are known for the warmth and luster of their wool, allowing many a colonist to survive inside hollow glaciers.

label: smoldersting scorpion
attackSummary: left claw(6p/2.6s); right claw(6p/2.6s); stinger(9p/1s); head(6p/2s)
description: This colossal scorpion is found only in the deepdest depths of the earth. It uses its burning venom to cook its prey alive from the inside out.

label: snowstalker
attackSummary: left claw(11p/1.5s); right claw(11p/1.5s); Bite(16p/2s); head(9p/2s)
description: One of the most dangerous big cats, snowstalker are solitary hunters with long, sharp teeth and claws. They stalk prey from hidden positions before pouncing.\n\nWhile humans are not their normal diet, they won't turn down a meal of vulnerable human meat.

label: sonar rabbit
description: The echolocation ability of this rabbit has enabled it to survive even in pitch-black environments. It tends to feed on and make its home within the smaller fungi of the underground.

label: stoneback
attackSummary: left claw(8p/2s); right claw(8p/2s); Bite(10p/2.6s); head(5p/2s)
description: These large reptile-like animals normally feed on the likes of cacti. If angered, however, their durable hide makes them quite difficult to kill.\n\nTheir longer back legs and strange appearance lends credence to the belief that they were engineered to live in arid environments. Why they live underground, however, is uncertain.

label: thrumbungus
attackSummary: mushrooms(23p/2.6s); ToxicBite(28p/2.6s); left paw(19p/6s); right foot(19p/6s); head(17p/6s)
description: A gigantic, fungal amalgam creature. Rumor in the UnderRim says it was created from a mix of a failed genetics experiment and the fungi that feasted on its corpse.\n\nWhile gentle by nature, it is dangerous when enraged. The strange hide that covers much of it is extremely beautiful and incredibly resistant to damage.

label: truffle mole
attackSummary: left claw(4p/1.5s); right claw(4p/1.5s); Bite(6p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: Thought to be related in some strange way to the truffle pigs of Earth, this mole has a specialized sense of smell, enabling it to find rare fungi.

label: woolly bat
description: These large bats have been farmed for their wool-like fur for generations. They were selectively bred to be flightless to make wool gathering easier. Their livable temperature range is shockingly wide.

label: xyrion
attackSummary: left claw(3p/2s); right claw(3p/2s); Bite(6p/2.6s); head(4p/2s)
description: This large reptile was first brought to Rimworlds as a strange pet due to its ability to lose its tail without harm, much like some geckos. Years after some were released or escaped into underground caverns, their preferred habitat, it was discovered that they can be raised and farmed for their surprisingly nutritious tails. Their tails begin to grow back immedately after removal but take days to

label: yooka
attackSummary: left hoof(8p/2s); right hoof(8p/2s); Bite(10p/5s); head(14p/5s)
description: A towering hunchbacked mammal closely related to camels and llamas. With little to no natural predators, it grazes among the taller fungi with an unconcerned grace.

label: crab
description: A crab

label: terrestrial octopus
description: This land-dwelling octopus has somehow adapted to being fully amphibious, able to survive for long periods out of the water. Much like other octopi, it predates on anything small enough.

label: maxolotl
attackSummary: left claw(9p/2s); right claw(9p/2s); Blunt(20p/2.6s); head(8p/2s)
description: These large salamanders prefer wet environments with pools of water they can comfortably slip into. While they lack teeth, their strong jaws can crush the shells of most insects. They are capable of fertilizing multiple batches of eggs in one go.

label: rose flamingo
description: Wading birds that get their color from the krill they eat by filtering food out of the water with their beaks. They thrive anywhere with warm, shallow water.

label: barbed pangolin
description: While passive in nature, this creature still has potent defenses. Its spiky plating has barbed edges, causing pain and bleeding to anything that tries to attack it and its tongue is covered with organic neurotoxins that cause rapid paralysis.

label: bilious varog
attackSummary: left claw(8p/2.6s); right claw(8p/2.6s); Bite(10p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: Adapted to disgustingly toxic waters, this relative of the common crocodile is highly dangerous when hungry. Alongside its razor sharp teeth, its powerful jaws also contain acid glands for drooling acid onto prey.

label: bloodletter petrel
description: Uniquely adapted amongst the other wild creatures in polluted environments. Rather than feeding off potentially toxic flesh or plant matter, it instead prefers to feed off the blood of its prey.

label: bunker bug
description: Whether it is engineered or mutated from a wild animal is unknown, but this massive insect-like creature can use its powerful claws to rend its way through steel almost as easily as flesh and bone. It does not breed in captivity.

label: carrion vulture
description: An eater of dead flesh, this bird will flock en masse to rotting corpses before bothering to hunt live prey.

label: pustule hornet
description: Predatory and dangerous, these hornets release toxic gas should they be harmed or killed. They defend their hives and their queen with considerable ferocity backed up by stings laced with potent neurotoxin.\n\nThey do not reproduce outside of their hives and give very little meat or chitin. This variety is loyal to the domesticated queen.

label: pustule queen
description: Unlike most other insect queens, this matriarch is very dangerous. She is nearly as fast as her spawn and packs a greater punch with her stings. Her stings inject a more potent version her species' neurotoxin, allowing for her swarm to quickly overpower anything living in their way.

label: mantrap
description: Massive compared to its progenitor, the venus flytrap, the mantrap is named such due to its ability to snag prey the size of humans. This variant has managed to develop proto-feet and can move very slowly to more food-rich environments. This all tends to terrify people.

label: famine locust
description: While small and weak, the famine locust can devastate colonies as easily as any raiders as they devour their way through fields of crops.

label: fenrid stoat
attackSummary: left claw(13p/1.5s); right claw(13p/1.5s); razorfangs(15p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: A large species of mustelid that can survive both toxic habitats as well as fights with most other native predators. Its preferred prey is varmots and they are often tamed for the express purpose of keeping varmots out of farms and granaries. It is known for digging up previously buried varmot corpses, much to the surprise of new tamers.

label: gastro toad
attackSummary: left claw(2p/2s); right claw(2p/2s); Bite(3p/2s); head(1p/2s)
description: A funny looking toad bigger than some rabbits. It uses its sticky acidic tongue and wide maw to snag small prey. Some waster colonies tame and raise them for their meat as well as the drug-like bile they produce.

label: glowtail
attackSummary: left claw(2p/2s); right claw(2p/2s); Bite(3p/2.6s); head(2p/2s)
description: A small lizard adapted to toxic environments, it uses its glowing tail tip to lure in flying insects to eat. It's considered rather cute by denizens of polluted lands and is often kept as both pet and pest control, much like a cat.

label: lyncus seal
description: Intelligent but territorial when it comes to its own species, lyncus seal males will try to kill each other almost on sight. Clubbing its babies is not a good idea.

label: maligoat
description: Naturally so hideous and maligned for its looks that it makes people flinch and cringe on sight, it is not often kept as a farm animal. For those that do so however, it produces milk of a high quality not seen elsewhere.

label: megakrill
description: While much larger than traditional krill, the megakrill is nearly as harmless. It eats algae and the like from polluted ponds and rivers. Some colonies keep swarms of them in ponds as emergency food.

label: megaphorid
description: A glass cannon of a creature, this disgusting bug attacks animals many times its size and tends to die in the process. Unbeknownst to the attacked, they have usually been injected with the phorid's young, which will slowly devour them from the inside out. It can survive in all but the most cold and barren environments.

label: megaphorid maggot
description: The larval form of the megaphorid fly. It is extremely ravenous and not very dangerous on its own, but they are rarely if ever found as such. They are most often found having burst out of an infected animal.

label: megaroach
description: This small, solitary roach can survive in nearly any polluted environment. While most roaches are considered pests, this species actually keeps colonies it lives in cleaner by chowing down on all kinds of filth.

label: mucklurker catfish
description: Huge yet slow, the mucklurker catfish waits along the filthy bottom of waterways for its prey to come to it, luring them in using the glowing tips of its whiskers.

label: mutagenic norphea
description: This unique insectoid's body is so adapted to environmental toxins that it cannot survive without them. It periodically produces a liquid that can induce mutations in humans.

label: mutating tumorfish
description: The adult form of the tumorfish. Now adapted to an amphibious lifestyle, it can hunt in water as well as on land. Despite still being quite fishy, it can move with surprising dexterity out of water.

label: mutating tumorfish fry
description: The second life stage of the tumorfish. It is now bigger and omnivorous, strong enough to hunt when necessary.

label: mutating tumorfish spawn
description: The first stage of the tumorfish life cycle. It is quite weak.

label: polluwog
description: The larval form of the gastro toad. It lives in the disgusting waters of polluted biomes, feeding off any detritus and plants it can reach. It often lives in large groups.

label: pustule hornet
description: Predatory and dangerous, these hornets release toxic gas should they be harmed or killed. They defend their hives and their queen with considerable ferocity backed up by stings laced with potent neurotoxin.\n\nThey do not reproduce outside of their hives and give very little meat or chitin.

label: pustule queen
description: Unlike most other insect queens, this matriarch is very dangerous. She is nearly as fast as her spawn and packs a greater punch with her stings. Her stings inject a more potent version her species' neurotoxin, allowing for her swarm to quickly overpower anything living in their way. The sheer bulk of her body prevents especially long active flights, forcing her to slow her movement for longer peri

label: pustule hornet
description: Predatory and dangerous, these wasps release toxic gas should they be killed. They defend their hives and their queen with considerable ferocity backed up by stings laced with potent neurotoxin.\n\nThey do not reproduce outside of their hives and give very little meat or chitin.

label: sacapillar
description: Timid by nature, this larva-like bug has a large thorax filled with putrescent gasses, allowing it to move about and escape attackers while barely touching the ground. It releases these gasses when attacked, often allowing it to escape unharmed. The gasses it contains also permit it to carry large loads, and many colonies in polluted areas use them as ridable pack animals.

label: screecher
description: Mutated by pollution, this corvid has gained the ability to stun its prey using its cries while it attacks. It tends to hunt in packs.

label: sludgecrawler
description: A gigantic mutant snail with two heads. It uses its unique slime for defense, as it rapidly hardens into something akin to biological cement.

label: smog moth
description: A large moth with wings with markings that glow faintly in the dark. This creature uses its bioluminescent abdomen to lure in prey.

label: smog caterpillar
description: The larval form of the smog moth. To deter predators, it uses toxic colors.

label: smog pupa
description: The pupal form of the smog moth. While immobile, its hard shell and terrible taste protects it from most predators.

label: swarmcaller
description: Found only in polluted areas, this insectoid feeds on otherwise inedible toxic waste. Unfortunately for any humanoids around it, eating said waste tends to lure in other insectoids.

label: tainted turtle
description: A mutated turtle that can withstand the noxious waters of polluted biomes. It cannot however survive its own toxin-filled sacs bursting due to high stress.

label: tox-wool sheep
attackSummary: head(12p/2.8s); left hoof(5p/2s); right hoof(5p/2s); Bite(12p/2s)
description: Most sheep produce wool, but only this breed produces wool that absorbs toxins, allowing unmodified humans to survive for longer in polluted lands were they to wear clothes made from it.

label: triple snapper
description: With three heads comes the ability to attack fast and see in almost every direction. The triple snapper is an apex predator of polluted waters. It cannot, however, move very fast on land.

label: varmot
description: A small herbivore that can often be found near human settlements in colder climates. For some reason, it tries to get towards human crops and stored food before any local plants.

label: waste hound
attackSummary: left claw(13p/1.5s); right claw(13p/1.5s); razorfangs(15p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: Despite its gaunt and somewhat haggard appearance, the wastehound is both agile and potentially dangerous for anyone that angers one, even moreso should it have a pack backing it up. Its speed is enhanced by the toxins found in pollution.

label: agrihand
description: A small mechanoid designed to sow and harvest crops. While it is better suited to labor than combat, it can fight with built-in cutting blades if necessary.

label: apocriton
description: A mechanoid commander designed to coordinate and motivate other mechs during long extermination campaigns. Its most obvious power is its ability to resurrect recently-killed mechs by supercharging their self-repair processes. Less obviously, it is intelligent and psychically present, radiating hatred into the minds of anyone in a wide radius. It can also move quickly with its built-in jump launche

label: centurion
description: An ultraheavy mech with a built-in shield bubble generator. The centurion carries a point-defense bulb turret capable of firing while the mechanoid is moving.

label: cleansweeper
description: A light mechanoid designed for cleaning. Lacking a ranged weapon, it can make only weak melee attacks.

label: constructoid
description: A small mechanoid designed to perform construction tasks. It can perform blunt melee attacks if necessary.

label: diabolus
description: An ultra-heavy mechanoid with an ultra-powerful hellsphere cannon. Made for siegebreaking, its hellsphere cannon takes time to charge up a shot, but can melt concrete and vaporize bone. The diabolus dissipates the hellsphere cannon's waste power in a heat column mounted on its back, which can pulse to ignite flammable objects nearby.\n\nThis mech's name comes from a thousand-year-old poem written

label: fabricor
description: A small work mechanoid designed to craft all manner of manufactured objects.

label: legionary
description: A combat support mechanoid with a wide-range bullet shield and mid-range needle gun. Designed to support other mechanoids, the legionary is vulnerable to anyone who can get inside its shield.

label: lifter
description: A small mechanoid designed for hauling. Lacking a ranged weapon, it can make only weak melee attacks.

label: militor
description: A small combat mechanoid armed with a low-power mini-shotgun. Roughly four feet tall, militors lack the power, range, and toughness of more senior combat mechs. However, it is cheap to gestate and maintain, and so is often used as a rear guard or swarm attacker.\n\nIn war, mech armies are known to send militors into urban ruins to hunt down survivors after breaking the human defenses. For this rea

label: paramedic
description: A small mechanoid designed for non-violent emergency situation management and medical care. The paramedic can rescue the wounded, fight fires, treat the sick, and even perform surgery when a more-qualified human is not available. Its built-in jump launcher allows it to jump into, and out of, emergency situations, and its built-in firefoam popper can quickly extinguish fires.

label: scorcher
attackSummary: front left leg(12.0p/2s); front right leg(12.0p/2s); head(8.5p/2s)
description: A close-approach war mechanoid that specializes in incendiary attacks. Its flame burst attack has little reach, but once it closes on a group of defenders it can ignite and disrupt them with blasts of searing flame.

label: tesseron
description: A medium-range combat mechanoid. While it is fairly vulnerable to attacks, the tesseron's sweeping beam graser can pierce thick armor and even ignite shielded targets.

label: tunneler
attackSummary: left power claw(22p/2.9s); right power claw(22p/2.9s)
description: A heavy mechanoid built for mining in treacherous locations. While intended for excavation, the tunneler's gigantic power claws and ultra-thick armor makes it a dangerous force in combat.

label: war urchin
description: A small, deployable combat mechanoid usually manufactured inside an ultra-heavy war queen mech. War urchins are expendable fighters designed to swarm-attack enemies. They are mounted with short-ranged spiner guns and have a non-rechargeable power source.

label: war queen
description: An ultra-heavy mech with a built-in mech gestator. Fed with appropriate resources, the war queen can form small war urchin combat mechs within its massive carapace and deploy them into combat.\n\nEven more than other mechanoids, the war queen resembles a giant, living insect. All war mechs can be terrifying, but humans tend to find the war queen disturbing on a deeper level.

label: toxalope
attackSummary: head(7p/2s); left hoof(9p/2s); right hoof(9p/2s); Bite(10p/2s)
description: A pollution-adapted cousin of the boomalope, the toxalope grows toxic pouches on its back. When it dies, the toxic material explodes and produces a deadly toxic cloud. Unlike the boomalope, the toxalope cannot be milked.

label: waste rat
attackSummary: left claw(3.6p/1.5s); right claw(3.6p/1.5s); ToxicBite(6p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: A toxin-adapted variant of the common rat. Waste rats have evolved to be pollution-resistant, as well as larger, tougher, and more aggressive than standard rats. Their bite infects their attacker with toxic buildup.

label: summoned scyther
description: Fast, spindly, human-sized combat mechanoids specializing in rapid approach and close-range combat. Their bodies are covered in points and blades, but they mostly use their two arm blades to lop off limbs or gut their victims alive.

label: cephalope
description: Descended from squid this tentacled monstrosity is like a spider the size of a deer. Fast and aggressive with a lethal bite delivered by venomous beak. An internal shell protects their vital organs.

label: landopus
description: Despite the name, this bad-tempered creature evolved from squid and has eight tentacles and two arms. The landopus has a venomous bite and a full load of its deadly neurotoxin will kill a healthy adult human in a minute or less.

label: nautilant
description: These armored behemoths are ambush predators, using their powerful tentacles to snatch prey and deliver a venomous bite. Their limestone shells are self-contained ecosystems of stored water and symbiotic algae that can keep the enormous mollusc alive in almost any environment.

attackSummary: left claw(17p/2s); right claw(17p/2s); Bite(23.6p/2.6s); head(11p/2s)
left claw(11p/1.5s); right claw(11p/1.5s); Bite(16p/2s); head(9p/2s)

description: Heavy combat mechanoids that glide on dozens of tiny legs. Their thick carapace and firepower makes them very effective against bunched-up static defenders. They are somewhat vulnerable to mobile hit-and-run tactics.

attackSummary: left claw(8p/2s); right claw(8p/2s); Bite(9p/2s); head(4p/2s)
left claw(10.9p/2s); right claw(10.9p/2s); Bite(12p/2s); head(6p/2s)

label: alpaca
attackSummary: left hoof(7.3p/2s); right hoof(7.3p/2s); Bite(8p/2s); head(7p/2s)
description: A medium-sized ungulate closely related to the llama, the alpaca is usually raised for its remarkably soft and insulating wool. Alpacas have also been used as pack animals since they hauled cargo on the rugged mountain trails of ancient South America.

label: alphabeaver
attackSummary: left claw(7.2p/2s); right claw(7.2p/2s); Bite(8.5p/2s); head(3p/2s)
description: A large beaver-like creature genetically engineered to harvest wood with machine-like efficiency. In the absence of specialized feed, these animals will enter a manic state that compels them to eat trees whole, and are likely to attack if disturbed.

label: grizzly bear
attackSummary: left claw(17p/2s); right claw(17p/2s); Bite(23.6p/2.6s); head(11p/2s)
description: A huge omnivorous mammal adapted for cold climates. Bears' thick blubber and fur keeps them warm in winter.\n\nWhile their usual diet consists of fish, berries, honey, and scavenged meat, the grizzly is capable of using its massive strength and deadly claws to kill live prey. They are startlingly quick for such lumbering creatures.

label: polar bear
attackSummary: left claw(17p/2s); right claw(17p/2s); Bite(23.6p/2.6s); head(11p/2s)
description: A great white bear adapted for frozen climates. Their thick blubber and fur keep them warm in winter.\n\nWhile their usual diet consists of fish and scavenged meat, the polar bear can also use its massive strength and deadly claws to kill live prey. They are startlingly quick for such lumbering creatures.

label: bison
attackSummary: head(15p/2.9s); left hoof(10p/2s); right hoof(10p/2s); Bite(10p/2s)
description: A large plant eating mammal appearing in the savannah wilderness. Tamed are quite docile, but enraged are fast and dangerous.

label: boomalope
attackSummary: head(7p/2s); left hoof(9p/2s); right hoof(9p/2s); Bite(10p/2s)
description: Engineered for chemicals production, the boomalope grows a large sac of volatile chemicals on its back. Though it is weak and fragile for its size, other animals have learned to avoid it because of the huge explosion it produces when it dies. It can be milked to produce chemfuel - very carefully.

label: boomrat
attackSummary: left claw(5.4p/1.5s); right claw(5.4p/1.5s); Bite(4.9p/2s); head(3p/2s)
description: Either by deliberate genetic weaponization, or as an unusual defense mechanism, these rodent-like creatures create a powerful fire-starting explosion when killed.

label: capybara
attackSummary: left claw(8.4p/2s); right claw(8.4p/2s); Bite(8.5p/2s); head(4p/2s)
description: The largest natural rodent, the capybara is well-adapted for steaming jungle environments.

label: caribou
attackSummary: left hoof(10p/2s); right hoof(10p/2s); Bite(10p/2s); head(13p/2.6s)
description: A large member of the deer family, well-adapted to life in cold climates. Caribou can be milked, but refuse to carry packs.

label: cassowary
description: A large flightless bird with brightly-colored feathers. While it looks beautiful, its kick is vicious. It's known for being quick to aggression when harmed by violence or confronted by incompetent animal tamers.

label: cat
attackSummary: left claw(6p/1.5s); right claw(6p/1.5s); Bite(7p/2s); head(3p/2s)
description: One of mankind's first pets, the cat is a small mammal which hunts vermin. Known for their aloofness, cats are nevertheless popular companions because of their independence, calm disposition, and fine, pettable fur.

label: chicken
description: The most traditional farm bird, the chicken is raised for its eggs and meat. It grows very quickly and lays eggs very often.

label: chinchilla
attackSummary: left claw(3.6p/1.5s); right claw(3.6p/1.5s); Bite(5.8p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: A small, nimble rodent. Its fur is softer than just about anything in the universe, making it very valuable as a trade good.

label: cobra
description: A large predatory snake. Cobras can be highly aggressive if provoked, and their bite injects toxic venom into the victim.

label: cougar
attackSummary: left claw(11p/1.5s); right claw(11p/1.5s); Bite(16p/2s); head(9p/2s)
description: One of the most dangerous big cats, cougars are solitary hunters with long, sharp teeth and claws. They stalk prey from hidden positions before pouncing.\n\nWhile humans are not their normal diet, they won't turn down a meal of vulnerable human meat.

label: cow
attackSummary: Bite(8.8p/2.6s); head(7p/2s); left hoof(8p/2s); right hoof(8p/2s)
description: A large domesticated ungulate, cows have been bred for millennia to produce huge amounts of milk, meat, and leather. They are exceptionally gentle creatures and will never seek revenge, no matter how many times they are harmed. Most of them are so adapted to farm life that they cannot survive in the wild.

label: deer
attackSummary: left hoof(7p/2s); right hoof(7p/2s); teeth(8p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: A medium-sized herding herbivore which prefers to live in mixed forests and plains. Deer are very quick.

label: donkey
attackSummary: head(12p/2.9s); left hoof(8p/2s); right hoof(8p/2s); Bite(6p/2s)
description: A small relative of the horse, domesticated in ancient times for farm work. Its goofy call is simultaneously annoying and endearing.\n\nWhen in a caravan, people can ride donkeys to increase the caravan's speed.

label: dromedary
attackSummary: left hoof(9p/2s); right hoof(9p/2s); Bite(10p/2s); head(7p/2s)
description: A large land mammal adapted to arid environments. Domesticated since ancient times, its leather is exceptionally good at insulating against the desert heat, and its milk is quite nourishing. It can be used as a pack animal and mount, but its bouncing gait makes it slower to ride than a horse.\n\nBy storing water in its large humps and reclaiming moisture from its breath as it exhales, it can go we

label: duck
description: A very common type of farm bird, also appearing in the wild, the duck is raised for its delicious meat. It grows quick but lays eggs quite rarely.

label: elephant
attackSummary: tusk(25p/2.6s); left foot(16.9p/2s); right foot(16.9p/2s); head(14p/2s)
description: The largest unmodified land animal. Elephants have a long trunk they use to manipulate objects, and sharp tusks they use to gore attackers. A dead elephant's valuable tusks can be recovered by butchering it.\n\nIntelligent creatures with complex social relationships, elephants can be used as pack animals or trained to carry out the most complex of tasks. They live a long time, and are known to rem

label: elk
attackSummary: left hoof(10p/2s); right hoof(10p/2s); Bite(10p/2s); head(13p/2.6s)
description: A large member of the deer family, well-adapted to life in cold climates. Domesticated elk can be milked, but refuse to carry packs.

label: emu
description: A large flightless bird with beady eyes on its ugly face. With its bad attitude, it is the jerk of the natural world. Bother it, and it is guaranteed to seek revenge.

label: arctic fox
attackSummary: left claw(8p/2s); right claw(8p/2s); Bite(9p/2s); head(4p/2s)
description: A small predator adapted for cold climates. It usually hunts small game like mice and voles, sometimes burrowing through a meter of snow to reach its prey.

label: fennec fox
attackSummary: left claw(8p/2s); right claw(8p/2s); Bite(9p/2s); head(4p/2s)
description: A small fox originally from the northern part of Earth's Africa continent. It hunts small creatures and has very large ears for cooling itself in the heat.

label: red fox
attackSummary: left claw(8p/2s); right claw(8p/2s); Bite(9p/2s); head(4p/2s)
description: A small solitary canine evolved for hunting small prey in temperate climates. Chicken farmers hate foxes because of their ability to destroy a whole coop in minutes.

label: gazelle
attackSummary: left hoof(5.5p/1.5s); right hoof(5.5p/1.5s); Bite(7p/2s); head(7p/2s)
description: A small, extremely quick antelope known for its amazingly long leap.

label: goat
description: Naturally curious about the world, goats are among the friendliest domesticated creature bred by mankind.

label: goose
description: A domesticated bird kept by humans as poultry for it's eggs and meat. Lays eggs very often, however they take a long time to hatch.

label: guinea pig
attackSummary: left claw(3.6p/1.5s); right claw(3.6p/1.5s); Bite(5.8p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: Neither a pig or a creature from Guinea, these little rodents are bred to be a household pet and a delicious dinner.

label: hare
description: This small, solitary herbivore can swiftly hop away from danger.

label: horse
attackSummary: head(10p/2.9s); left hoof(7p/2s); right hoof(7p/2s); Bite(5p/2s)
description: A large hoofed mammal with a short coat, a long mane, and a long tail. Horses have been domesticated since ancient times.\n\nWhen in a caravan, people can ride horses to increase the caravan's speed.

label: human
attackSummary: left fist(8.2p/2s); right fist(8.2p/2s); teeth(8.2p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: A baseline human, mostly unmodified by gene engineering and mostly unchanged by evolutionary pressures on non-Earth planets.

label: husky
attackSummary: left claw(9.7p/2s); right claw(9.7p/2s); Bite(14.2p/2.6s); head(6p/2s)
description: A large, energetic dog with a thick fur coat for remaining comfortable in arctic environments.

label: ibex
attackSummary: left hoof(8p/2s); right hoof(8p/2s); Bite(8p/2s); head(10p/2.6s)
description: The wild ancestor of the domesticated goat. Ibexes live on marginal territory where most antelopes couldn't survive, eating lichens and sparse mountain plants. They're famous for dextrously hopping across bare cliff faces - and for their violent ramming attack.

label: iguana
attackSummary: left claw(8p/2s); right claw(8p/2s); Bite(10p/2.6s); head(5p/2s)
description: These large lizards normally feed on plant matter. However, when angered, their tough hide and sharp claws make them quite dangerous.\n\nResting iguanas hold their heads high, giving them an amusing 'proud' look. But they're not proud; they're just trying to see predators so they don't get eaten.

label: labrador retriever
attackSummary: left claw(8.5p/2s); right claw(8.5p/2s); Bite(14.2p/2.6s); head(5p/2s)
description: A very versatile, medium-sized dog. Originally bred to retrieve birds shot on the hunt, the lab is also an excellent guard dog, play pal, and family friend.

label: lynx
attackSummary: left claw(9p/1.5s); right claw(9p/1.5s); Bite(12p/2s); head(6p/2s)
description: A wildcat larger than a housecat, but smaller than a cougar. Lynxes survive on a diet of small birds and animals. Their very warm fur keeps them safe from the brutally cold temperatures of their frozen territories.

label: lancer
description: Fast human-sized combat mechanoids built for medium and long-range combat. Their bodies are light, making them vulnerable targets at close range - especially in melee combat.

label: pikeman
attackSummary: front left leg(12.0p/2s); front right leg(12.0p/2s); head(8.5p/2s)
description: A clunky multi-legged combat mechanoid specialized as a long-range weapons platform. While effective at distance, it is weak in close-range fights and in melee combat.\n\nVeterans of mechanoid wars know that often, the safest place to be around a pikeman is touching it.

label: scyther
description: Fast, spindly, human-sized combat mechanoids specializing in rapid approach and close-range combat. Their bodies are covered in points and blades, but they mostly use their two arm blades to lop off limbs or gut their victims alive.

label: termite
description: A medium-sized mechanoid. Termites specialize in burrowing, digging, and breaking through defensive structures. Defenders need to decide whether to try to eliminate the termite before it can dig through their defenses, or take it where it emerges.

label: megascarab
description: A large, genetically-engineered beetle. Once the worker caste of an artificial ecosystem of insectoids designed to fight mechanoid invasions, it is now often seen without its deadlier insectoid cousins. Still, its size and hard shell make it dangerous when it attacks. A eusocial creature, it cannot reproduce individually.

label: megasloth
attackSummary: left claw(21p/2s); right claw(21p/2s); Bite(22p/2.6s); head(15p/2s)
description: A giant, solitary herbivore with two giant claws for warding off threats. Long extinct after being wiped out by the natives of Earth's American continent, the megasloth was later brought back using advanced cloning and artificial gestators. Its thick hide is exceptionally strong and insulating, and makes a great leather for cold-weather clothing. It is peaceful if left alone, but will shred anyone

label: megaspider
description: Not actually a spider, the megaspider is a genetically-engineered giant insectoid the size of a small bear. Designed for heavy work and combat, its thick chitinous armor makes it hard to kill, while its long ripper-blades make it deadly at close quarters. It is, however, quite slow in open terrain.

label: monkey
attackSummary: left fist(3.6p/1.5s); right fist(3.6p/1.5s); Bite(4p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: A small primate, the monkey can use its curly tail to grab on to branches, leaving its hands free to do other things. Monkeys are selfish but clever, and can be trained to carry out fairly complex tasks.

label: muffalo
attackSummary: head(13p/2.6s); left hoof(10p/2s); right hoof(10p/2s); Bite(10p/2s)
description: A large herding herbivore descended from buffalo and adapted for both cold and warm environments. While enraged muffalo are deadly, tamed muffalo are quite docile and can be used as pack animals.\n\nNobody is quite sure why they're blue - it might even be some early genetic modification test that just never got changed.

label: ostrich
description: The largest unmodified bird species, ostriches are known for their fast run, huge eggs, and powerful kick. It is easily angered.

label: pig
description: Pigs were one of the first animals domesticated by humans. They are an efficient source of meat, and are easy to feed because they will eat almost anything.

label: raccoon
attackSummary: left claw(6p/2s); right claw(6p/2s); Bite(7p/2s); head(3p/2s)
description: A small, hardy animal that ranges wide across forests and shrubland. It is happy to break into your garbage container, or your kitchen, to eat almost anything.

label: rat
attackSummary: left claw(3.6p/1.5s); right claw(3.6p/1.5s); Bite(6p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: A widely-hated rodent known for soiling kitchens and spreading disease, rats have a way of following humans everywhere they go. It eats almost anything and lives almost anywhere.

label: rhinoceros
description: Despite being herbivorous, this large mammal is very easy to enrage. Once angered, its massive strength and sharp horn make it a brutal opponent. It has more muscle in one leg than most humans do in their whole body.

label: sheep
attackSummary: head(14p/2.9s); left hoof(6p/2s); right hoof(6p/2s); Bite(8p/2s)
description: Sheep husbandry is practiced throughout the majority of the inhabited worlds, however only recently it has been introduced to the rimworlds. Domestic sheep are relatively small herbivores, usually with yellowish wool and medium sized horns.

label: snowhare
description: This hardy animal survives the brutal winters of its homelands by burrowing through snow to find edible plants.

label: spelopede
description: A medium-sized bioengineered insectoid the size of a sheep. The spelopede is the middle caste of a hive, taking care of most work tasks as well as fighting with its digging claws. It's dangerous in combat, but slow on open ground.

label: squirrel
attackSummary: left claw(4p/2s); right claw(4p/2s); Bite(5p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: One of the many hardy rodent species that follows humankind everywhere it spreads. Squirrels are distinguished by their bushy tails, which they use as umbrellas in bad weather.

label: thrumbo
attackSummary: horn(23p/2s); Bite(28p/2.6s); left foot(19p/2s); right foot(19p/2s); head(17p/2s)
description: A gigantic, graceful creature of unknown origin. The thrumbo is gentle by nature, but extremely dangerous when enraged. While its long fur is exceptionally beautiful, its hide is also incredibly resistant to damage. Its razor-sharp horn fetches a huge price.\n\nLegends say that an old thrumbo is the wisest creature in the universe - it simply chooses not to speak.

label: tortoise
description: This heavily armored land-dwelling reptile is known for its slow moving speed and surprisingly vicious bite. Because of its natural armor, it is tough to kill and can do serious damage during drawn-out melee fights.

label: turkey
description: A short, fat, flightless bird known for its hilarious 'gobbling' call. It has been long domesticated, but also lives in the wild.

label: warg
attackSummary: left claw(13p/1.5s); right claw(13p/1.5s); razorfangs(15p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: Heavily-muscled wolf-like creatures with vicious unnatural claws and an absurdly powerful bite. They will only eat meat or corpses. If disturbed in the wild, they are very likely to attack.\n\nScientists say wargs are the descendants of weaponized military animals created for population suppression. The superstitious see them as the tools of an angry god.

label: wild boar
description: This hairy omnivore is descended from escaped pigs and evolved for living in the wild.\n\nIts tusks make it a better fighter than its domesticated pig cousins. Unfortunately, it is too unruly to be trained in the most complex tasks.

label: arctic wolf
attackSummary: left claw(10.9p/2s); right claw(10.9p/2s); Bite(12p/2s); head(6p/2s)
description: An arctic variant of the old Earth wolf. As pack hunters, wolves have a complex social life and are fiercely intelligent.

label: timber wolf
attackSummary: left claw(10.9p/2s); right claw(10.9p/2s); Bite(12p/2s); head(6p/2s)
description: A rugged predator long feared by many ancient Earth cultures. As pack hunters, wolves have complex social lives and are fiercely intelligent.

label: yak
attackSummary: Bite(8.8p/2.6s); head(9p/2s); left hoof(8p/2s); right hoof(8p/2s)
description: Yaks are robust cattle with a bulky frame, short but thick legs, and rounded cloven hooves that are splayed to help them walk in snow.

label: yorkshire terrier
attackSummary: left claw(3.6p/2s); right claw(3.6p/2s); cute little teeth(4.8p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: A small, even-tempered dog. Originally bred to hunt rats, it later became a show and companionship animal. Some consider it useless, but the mood boost it gives by nuzzling can outweigh the cost of feeding it.

attackSummary: left claw(20p/2s); right claw(20p/2s); beak(23.6p/2.6s); head(17p/2.2s)
left claw(7p/1.5s); right claw(7p/1.5s); beak(8p/1.5s); head(3p/2.2s)

label: arctic owlcat
attackSummary: left claw(7p/1.5s); right claw(7p/1.5s); beak(8p/1.5s); head(3p/2.2s)
description: A strange creature combining the features of a feline and that of an owl. The nimble predator referred only as owlcats can be commonly found hunting and nesting in the woodlands. Their long elegant wings are vestigial and primarly serve in the mating season, in order to attract new partners or to scare off predators by appearing bigger than they are.\n\nAdapted to the frozen climates, the arctic o

label: barogoth
attackSummary: head(13p/2.6s); left claw(10p/2s); right claw(10p/2s); Bite(10p/2s)
description: A large herbivorous amphibian that thrives in humid environments. Barogoth are often found near swamps and wetlands, where they will mate and lay eggs for the great majority of their lives. Quite docile when tamed, they are regularly used as pack animals.\n\nBarogoth secrete a thick oily liquid that can be collected and used as a medicinal ointment. While applied on the body, it increase one's rec

label: bearded troll
attackSummary: head(12p/2s); left claw(16p/2s); right claw(16p/2s); Bite(23p/2.4s)
description: This large, eyeless predator roams the frigid landscape, constantly in search of food. During winter, they often retreat deep into underground burrows, to feast on the many corpses they hoarded throughout the rest of the year. Relentless and capable of quickly regenerating its wounds, it allows the trolls to take down creatures much stronger than itself.\n\nTrolls spread quickly and are considered

label: black scribe
attackSummary: left pincer(9p/1.5s); right pincer(9p/1.5s); DA_Quillsting(13p/2s); head(4p/2s)
description: A shade amongst the scorching sands. The black scribe is a deadly insectoid capable of taking down creatures much larger than itself with its dreadful sting. The name of scribe comes from its feather-like stinger, composed of countless small quills that it uses to quickly inject a toxic venom, which greatly weakens its prey.\n\nIt’s venom can be safely extracted every few days, and while the toxin

label: crestel
description: One of the largest flightless birds, and the north's apex predator. The crestel is a fearsome beast that can completely paralyze unfortunate victims for a short duration with its venomous beak, rendering them helpless against its attacks. label: Stygimoloch
description: -- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #03521-1931 [STYGIMOLOCH SPINIFER] CODENAME: STYX >9482 A pachycephalosaurid with a thick dome and a mottled cream and blue hide. Their calls have made them a nuisance, so much so small tribal villages will actively ward them away, lest they attract larger threats.

label: Styracosaurus
description: -- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #039902-1913 [STYRACOSAURUS ALBERTENSIS] CODENAME: STYRAX >230 A ceratopsian well known for the multitude of spikes decorating its head. Smaller than most ceratopsians, they often use their lesser stature for speed rather than strength.

label: Suchomimus
description: -- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #01997-1998 [SUCHOMIMUS TENERENSIS] CODENAME: SCYTHE >17 A spinosaurid with an agressive temper and a crooked, teeth riddled maw. Their arched neck allows them to strike quickly, and their claws are perfect for slicing up fish - or colonists.

label: Supersaurus
description: -- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #03927-1985 [SUPERSAURUS VIVIANAE] CODENAME: MONUMENT >908 A beautiful sauropod with a jade-like hide. Gathering in large herds, these massive creatures spend the majority of the day grazing to sate their hearty appetite.

label: Tenontosaurus
description: -- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #02321-1970 [TENONTOSAURUS TILLETTI] CODENAME: SINEW >412 A large ornithopod with a slender, elongated tail, theorized to have acted as a whip with which it attacked predators, or perhaps other unruly herd members. They are often preyed upon by dinosaurs which hunt in packs.

label: Termitotron
description: -- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #04821-2014 [TERMITOTRON VENDEENSE] CODENAME: DAMPWOOD >4910 A rather large and nasty species of proto-termite. Their insatiable appetite for wood wouldn't be so bad if their extremely powerful, clicking manidibles couldn't cut through walls and workbenches as if they were made of tissue paper. Avoid at all costs.

label: Therizinosaurus

label: Triceratops
description: -- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #0481-1889 [TRICERATOPS HORRIDUS] CODENAME: TRINITY >526 An extremely famous ceratopsid dinosaur. Noble and proud, these incredible forces of nature have stood the test of time and intregrated well into the rim. They are well known for their bravery, and their supposed rivalry with Tyrannosaurus rex.

label: Troodon
description: -- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #IG74726f6f646f6e [TROODON PECTINODON] WOUNDING TOOTH Bred on Isla Sorna during the initial testing phase of Jurassic Park, Troodon were considered to be too dangerous for public display, and were ordered to be destroyed. description: -- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #03321-2007 [TUPANDACTYLUS IMPERATOR] CODENAME: SAIL >3729 A pterosaur with a big, rounded crest. These crest are often more colourful and larger in males, possibly to impress mates when the time comes.

description: -- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #09182-1905[TYRANNOSAURUS REX] CODENAME: KING >1 The king tyrant lizard. Boasting incredible power, tenacity and speed, this dinosaur has earned its namesake. It was responsible for much chaos on the mainland of San Fransico during the 1997 incident, where it was revealed it had wreaked havoc prior on Isla Nublar during 1994.

label: wonambi
description: -- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #00211-1976 [WONAMBI NARACOORTENSIS] CODENAME: RIVERSLEIGH >932 Wonambi was a genus of non-venomous, constrictor snakes, and seems to have been an ambush predator that killed its prey by constriction. The head of the animal was small, restricting the size of its prey.

label: Yangchuanosaurus
description: -- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #0498-1978 [YANGCHUANOSAURUS SHANGYOUENSIS] CODENAME: LAZULI >472 A metriacanthosaurid theropod with a spotty blue hide. They are a fierce predator, their huge size allowing them to overpower many different species of prey.

description: A genetically-modified variant of the kangaroo rat. They are capable of subsisting off of water created by their metabolism, allowing them to survive in even the most extreme of hot environments.

label: kangaroo rat
attackSummary: left claw(1p/1.5s); right claw(1p/1.5s); Bite(1.5p/2s); head(0.5p/2s)
description: An odd rodent fond of warmer climates and seeds. They are capable of subsisting off of water created by their metabolism, allowing them to survive in even the most dry environments.

label: lemming
attackSummary: left claw(1p/1.5s); right claw(1p/1.5s); Bite(1.5p/2s); head(0.5p/2s)
description: A small rodent fond of colder climates. They're a tasty snack for most predators!

label: mouse
attackSummary: left claw(1p/1.5s); right claw(1p/1.5s); Bite(1.5p/2s); head(0.5p/2s)
description: A smaller relative of the world-renowned rat. They have a habit of making their way into homes and feeding on the contents of your pantry. It might be a good idea to keep a cat or two around...

label: poison mouse
attackSummary: left claw(1p/1.5s); right claw(1p/1.5s); Bite(1.5p/2s); head(0.5p/2s)
description: A smaller relative of the world-renowned rat, although this one looks a bit odd. They have a habit of making their way into homes and feeding on the contents of your pantry. It might be a good idea to keep a cat or two around...

label: andrewsarchus
description:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

This mysterious carnivore was the biggest predatory mammal of its time.
Often described as a "bear-dog", it was apparently related to entelodonts, hippopotamuses, and whales.

label: arthropleura
description:
Long extinct giant arthropods, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The largest known land invertebrate of all time. Arthropleuras are huge, solitary, herbivorous millipedes that are mostly harmless, and will attack only in self-defense.
Some maniacs are willing to pay unreasonable amounts of money for eggs of this beast.

label: aurochs
attackSummary: left hoof(10p/1.65s); right hoof(10p/1.65s); horn(18p/1.35s); head(15p/1.65s)
description:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The ancestor of domestic cattle, the aurochs, was to modern cows what wolves are to dogs.
Larger, tougher, faster, but producing less resources and eating more than today's cattle.

label: castoroides
attackSummary: left claw(12p/1.5s); right claw(12p/1.5s); Bite(14p/1.75s); head(9p/2s)
description:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Giant beavers, the largest to ever exist.
