Its incisors aren't as well fitted for cutting wood as those of its modern equivalents, which is why it doesn't bother with constructing dams. This makes it so it will more often have to resort to either running from predators or attempting to fight them off, instead o

label: chalicotherium
description:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Despite what its bizzare appearance could suggest, chalicotherium is most closely related to horses and rhinoceroses.
It walks on its knuckles and uses its huge sloth-like claws as both a rake and a mean of defense against predators.

label: daeodon
description: Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.\n\nDaeodons are large, pig-like, omnivorous animals. However, they are much more aggressive and dangerous than regular pigs or even wild boars. Try to stay away from their gigantic maws.

label: deinotherium
attackSummary: tusk(34p/2.3s); left foot(18p/1.75s); right foot(18p/1.75s); head(15p/1.65s)
description:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

"Deinotherium" means "terrible beast". It's a unique cousin to mammoths and mastodons, equipped with downward curving tusks on the lower jaw.
Very short-tempered and incredibly dangerous when angered.

label: dinocrocuta
description:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Gigantic hyena-like predators. Their exceptionally strong jaws easily crush bones.
Extremely aggresive, it's known to surprisingly often prey on animals larger than itself.

label: dinopithecus
description:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

A gigantic species of baboons with an unusually prominent liking for meat.
They used to be the natural enemies of early humans, hunting them down more often than one could expect. It is possible that they could see modern humans as prey, too.

label: dinornis
description: Long extinct giant birds, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.\n\nThe tallest birds to ever exist. They belong to the moa family and are characterised by quite dramatic sexual dimorphism, with the females being significantly larger than the males

label: diprotodon
description:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The largest known marsupial to have ever lived. As huge as a rhinoceros, it resembles a gigantic wombat.
Diprotodon's a relatively peaceful creature, however its huge pair of forward-facing teeth as well as its strong claws can prove quite dangerous in a combat situation.

label: doedicurus
attackSummary: tail(25p/3s); left claw(10p/1.75s); right claw(10p/1.75s); Bite(16p/1.8s)
description:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The largest known glyptodont. Its huge carapace is nearly unbreakable to any predator. 
Even though the tip of its tail is covered in spikes and would thus make for a decent weapon, it cannot use it effectively due to its very limited field of vision.

label: elasmotherium
description: Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.\n\nThe largest horned rhinoceros of all time. Elasmotherium uses its giant singular horn, placed on its forehead, to fight, attract mates, sweep snow, and dig in the ground in search of water and plant roots.

label: enhydriodon
description:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The largest mustelid ever discovered. Enhydriodon is a bear-sized ancestor of modern otters, and a very dangerous predator that used to be a big threat to early humans.
Great swimmers, surprisingly swift on land.

label: gigantophis
description:
Long extinct giant reptiles, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The second biggest snake in history, thought to have been the largest until the discovery of titanoboa.
It much prefers hunting big animals as they're easier to smell out.

label: gigantopithecus
description: Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.\n\nGigantopithecus is the largest known ape that ever lived. They are highly intelligent, social creatures that feed on seeds and fruit. Thanks to their thick fur, they are quite resistant to cold - the lone specimens seen in the mountains are said to have been the inspiration to stories about the mythical Big Foo

label: gomphotaria
description:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Gomphotaria is equipped with not two, but four huge tusks that it uses to hammer and pierce its prey with.
Their seal-like bodies allow them to move very swiftly underwater but their huge mass as well as a lack of legs renders them somewhat sluggish on land.

label: josephoartigasia
description:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The largest rodent of all time, josephoartigasia, resembles a gigantic capybara or pacarana, but in a few regards it appears to be closer to today's hippopotamuses.
It is not a very good runner, and to compensate for that, it sports huge incisors that could prove very dangerous to lesser predators.

label: macrauchenia
description:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Despite it possessing a trunk, macrauchenia's nostrils are actually located on the top of its head.
It's extraordinarily agile and thanks to its ability of rapidly changing directions while running at high speed, it can escape most predators fairly easily.

label: megalania
description:
Long extinct giant reptiles, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The biggest terrestial lizard of all time, as well as the biggest venomous vertebrate that's ever existed.
Because of its relatively short legs, most of megalania's prey can easily outrun it, which is why it most often has to rely on the element of surprise in its hunts.

label: megaloceros
description:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Despite being colloquially known as the 'Giant Elk', it's, in fact, not an elk but an enormous deer.
Megaloceros is an easily angered herbivore that can cause severe wounds with its extraordinarily large antlers, which are otherwise used exclusively for attracting females.

label: megalochelys
description:
Long extinct giant reptiles, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The largest tortoise of all time.
There aren't many predators that pose a threat to megalochelys, thanks to its thick and hard as rock shell. The ones that attempt to attack it anyway, will have to be prepared to deal with its surprisingly powerful bite.

label: meganeura
description:
Long extinct giant arthropods, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The biggest flying insect to ever exist, meganeura, just like modern dragonflies, is a highly specialised predator.
Swift and agile, it used to have no aerial competition, which was one of the reasons why it had evolved to be so gigantic.

label: palaeeudyptes
description: Long extinct giant birds, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.\n\nThe biggest penguin in history. While it's clearly best fitted for hunting fish, palaeeudyptes won't hesitate to take advantage of its huge size, and will attempt to hunt other vertebrates that are smaller than itself.

label: paraceratherium
description:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The largest land mammal known to man, Paraceratherium, is a gentle creature, however its size alone can also make it quite a formidable foe to face.
Feeds on plants and trees, which it can easily reach with its extraordinarily long neck, the trait that makes it unique to other genera of rhinoceroses.

label: platybelodon
attackSummary: tusk(20p/2.5s); left foot(12p/1.85s); right foot(12p/1.85s); head(10p/1.85s)
description:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Very unique kind of proboscideans, which, due to the shape of their two lower teeth is popularly known as "shovel tuskers".
It grasps tree branches with its trunk and rubs them against the lower teeth to cut them off. The "tusk shovel" is also used by platybelodons to strip bark from trees.

label: procoptodon
attackSummary: feet(17p/1s); left fist(15p/1s); right fist(15p/1s); Bite(12p/1.6s)
description:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The largest known kangaroo that ever existed. Unlike its modern equivalents, procoptodons move around not by hopping but by walking, just like hominids.
They are very dangerous due to their ability to throw unbelievably swift punches.

label: pulmonoscorpius
attackSummary: left pincer(13p/1.25s); right pincer(13p/1.25s); stinger(17p/1.7s); Bite(13p/1.55s)
description:
Long extinct giant arthropods, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The biggest land scorpion to ever exist.
Pulmonoscorpius is a solitary predator capable of taking down creatures way larger than itself with its deadly venom. Its sting should be stayed away from at all costs.

label: purussaurus
description:
Long extinct giant reptiles, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Quite possibly, the largest crocodilian of all time, and also the biggest reptile to roam the Earth after the extinction of dinosaurs.
It is so massive that even giant ground sloths have a place on its menu.

label: quinkana
description:
Long extinct giant reptiles, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

This terrestrial crocodile possesses long legs, which render it much better of a runner than its modern equivalents.
Quinkana's teeth are shaped like knives, which makes them perfect for practically cutting away parts of its prey.

label: Short-faced bear
description: Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.\n\nOne of the largest, if not the largest bear in history. What stands out the most about its appearance is the disproportionately short snout compared to other bears and the extraordinarily long legs it possesses. The latter makes it so hardly any prey can effectively outrun it.

label: sivatherium
attackSummary: left hoof(13p/1.75s); right hoof(13p/1.75s); head(18p/1.65s); Bite(10p/1.7s)
description: Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.\n\nThe biggest ruminant in history. Unlike its modern equivalents, giraffes and okapis, sivatherium possesses two pairs of ossicones, one that is wide and resembles antlers, and the other being more horn-like, placed above its eyes.

label: smilodon
description: Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.\n\nSmilodon is an incredibly deadly predator, which kills its prey by holding it still with its strong forelimbs, and sinking its enormous pair of canines deep inside its neck.

label: titanis
description: Long extinct giant birds, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.\n\nColloquially known as terror birds, titanis are large carnivorous flightless birds. Their abnormally huge beaks are incredibly deadly, and their strong legs not only allow them to easily outrun their prey, but can also serve vicious kicks.

label: titanoboa
description: Long extinct giant reptiles, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.\n\nThe largest snake ever discovered, Titanoboa, is capable of swallowing cows whole. It can kill even medium-sized animals in just seconds, and thus should be stayed away from at all costs.

label: uintatherium
description:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

A very primitive, giant cousin of rhinoceroses.
It is neither the most beautiful, nor the most intelligent animal in history, with its brain being merely the size of an orange, but it can make up for it with its strong back, which renders it a good partner for a journey.

label: woolly mammoth
attackSummary: tusk(25p/2.2s); left foot(16p/1.65s); right foot(16p/1.65s); head(14p/1.65s)
description:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Very close relatives of modern elephants. Hunted by early humans for their meat, fur, and valuable tusks. 
As opposed to their today's equivalents, the mammoths' ears and tails are relatively short - to minimise frostbite and heat loss.

label: zygolophodon
attackSummary: tusk(33p/2.5s); left foot(18p/1.75s); right foot(18p/1.75s); head(14p/1.65s)
description:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

One of the mastodons, and owner of some of the longest tusks in history.
While more primitive than mammoths, it's bigger, tougher, and more powerful than most of them. It is also heavier than some sauropod dinosaurs.

label: Abomination
attackSummary: left fist(12.0p/2s); right fist(12.0p/2s); teeth(8.2p/2s); head(8.5p/2s)
description: Abominations are slow, hulking, relentless manifestations of flesh. Their bodies twist and contort to heal even major wounds quickly. Their mangled maw seeps with toxic bile. They will consume and assimilate, corpse by corpse.

label: aminox
description: Aminox are huge cold-climate herbivores descended from ancient muskox-like lineages. Their thick coats and natural endurance let them survive across tundras, frozen plains and regions where ordinary cattle would not last long.\n\nThe true value of the Aminox lies in its milk. Dense, nutritious and rich in unusual amino compounds, it sustains colonies in extreme environments and serves as the basis

label: Capryak
description: Capryaks are megagoats of the cold regions, adapted to tundras, frostbitten forests and mountainous terrain. Their dense coats, thick hides and long horns make them resistant to cold and difficult to bring down, especially when wounded.\n\nColonies can raise them for rugged wool, harsh but nourishing milk, and horns strong enough for primitive weapons. The problem is keeping them: because of their

label: deermoss
description: Deermoss are large forest herbivores covered in dense fur and symbiotic moss. They move silently through old woodlands and, though generally peaceful, their heavy frames and imposing antlers make them dangerous when threatened.\n\nTheir coats host medicinal vegetal fibers that can be harvested by careful handlers. They also produce a green, bitter and nutritious milk, but raising Deermoss is expen

label: direhorse
description: Direhorses are colossal ancestral horses covered in dense coats that protect them across frozen plains and harsh open country. Their herds move over great distances at a steady pace, keeping strength and endurance where lesser mounts would quickly wear down.\n\nOnce domesticated, a Direhorse becomes one of the most valuable caravan mounts on the frontier, combining speed, carrying capacity and bat

label: dunbear
description: Dunbears are ancient cave bears of monumental size, adapted to extreme cold and mountainous regions. They spend long periods in deep hibernation, waking with the thaw to roam the surface in search of food.\n\nHunting a Dunbear is a dangerous decision. Its mass, resilience and brute strength let it survive wounds that would drop most predators, while its dense and valuable fur makes it a tempting p

label: duskhorn
description: Duskhorns are ancient herd beasts known for their deep red coats and large ivory horns that recall the last light of day. They are commonly raised by tribes and frontier settlements for the value of their wool and the dense milk they produce.\n\nAlthough usually docile when kept in herds, duskhorns can become dangerous when wounded or when one of their own is threatened. Hunting them without prepa

label: furpotamus
description: Furpotamus are colossal, fur-covered ancestors of modern hippos, adapted to wetlands, swamps and cold riverbanks. Despite their heavy bodies, they move easily through flooded terrain and become far more dangerous near water.\n\nThey are herbivores, but territorial when harmed or pressured. Domestication is possible, though difficult due to their size, appetite and grazing needs. Hunters seek them

label: gnaut
description: Gnauts are large grazing animals, robust and social, reminiscent of ancient wildebeest and wild bovine stock. They live well in herds and fit naturally into open ecosystems, turning ordinary vegetation into meat, hide, bones and horns.\n\nThey provide no milk or wool, but make up for it through simplicity: domesticable animals useful to colonies that need a stable source of resources without relyi

label: harpeagle
description: Harpeagles are colossal birds of prey, large enough to cast shadows over herds and lift prey the size of a deer. They are feared by travelers and respected by tribes, not because they are sacred, but because few animals control the sky with such force.\n\nTheir feathers contain rare oils used to craft elixirs that sharpen the senses. Taming a Harpeagle is possible, but requires skill, courage and

label: Hellboar
attackSummary: Infectious bite(17p/2.2s); gnashing bite(12p/1.6s); crushing bite(28p/6.0s)
description: Hellboars are colossal omnivores drawn to blood, rot and abandoned flesh. They are not pure predators, but their constant hunger and brute strength make them willing to chase live prey when carrion and scraps grow scarce.\n\nThe greatest danger of a Hellboar is not only the impact of its charge, but its infectious bite. Its mouth carries enough filth, bacteria and rotting matter to turn a small wo

label: manehound
attackSummary: bite(18p/2.2s); left fang(14p/1.9s); right fang(14p/1.9s); head(11p/2.2s)
description: Manehounds are large feral guardian dogs descended from ancient cold-climate shepherd breeds. Their dense coats, heavy neck manes and watchful posture still reveal an animal made to stand between the herd and the threat.\n\nGenerations in the wild made them cautious and territorial, but never fully erased their domestic instincts. Unlike wolves or true hunting predators, Manehounds watch, endure a

label: narkospider
description: Narkospiders are massive subterranean spiders that hunt by ambush, preferring to sedate prey rather than overpower it through brute force. They wait in tunnels and dark spaces until a target comes close enough for a narcotic bite.\n\nTheir venom causes deep narkosis, reducing movement and perception until the victim can no longer respond. This makes the creature less explosive than other predators

label: Plastemmoth
description: Plastemmoths are colossal biometallic beasts that roam frozen and temperate regions. Their strength, resilience and body mass make them one of the most dangerous hunts on the frontier, especially when encountered moving with other members of the herd.\n\nOver a lifetime, plastite formations slowly grow within the body, shaped by biological processes and extreme environmental pressure. These unstab

label: Plastemmoth alpha
description: Plastemmoth Alphas are rare elder giants, larger and heavier than the rest of their species. They lead migrating herds through cold and temperate regions, carrying plastite plates so thick they seem fused into the skeleton itself.\n\nFacing an Alpha means facing the living center of the migration. Its natural carapace blunts common weapons, while the amount of plastite inside its body makes it one

label: raptorkhan
description: Raptorkhans are huge feathered terror birds, too fast for their size and intelligent enough to hunt in pairs. Without relying on flight, they dominate terrain through speed, strength and talons capable of tearing heavy protection.\n\nMated pairs are territorial, especially near nests and thick-shelled eggs. Their claws are valued by some cultures as material for ceremonial blades, but obtaining on

label: scarodon
attackSummary: left saber fang(24p/1.7s); right saber fang(24p/1.7s); claw swipe(18p/2.3s); punch(18p/3.2s)
description: Scarodons are solitary apex predators marked by saber-like fangs, robust bodies and thick fur covered in old scars. Roaming boreal and temperate forests, they are strong enough to hunt megafauna and dangerous enough to make even armed colonists hesitate.\n\nAlthough they eat almost anything, Scarodons seem to prefer large and valuable prey. Bringing one down can yield rare resources, including the

label: Simbakub
description: Simbakubs are large primitive lions, dangerous not only for their strength but for the way they hunt in packs. Across savannas, deserts and other harsh biomes, they stalk gnauts, direhorses and travelers, closing in silently before attacking as a group.\n\nWounding a single Simbakub can pull the entire pack into the fight. This collective response becomes even more dangerous in the presence of an

label: Simbakub Alpha
description: Simbakub Alphas are rare and immense individuals, strong enough to roam alone until they find or claim a new pack. Their roars mark wide territories, and few smaller predators remain nearby once an Alpha begins to hunt.\n\nWhen accepted by a pack, the Alpha becomes leader, protector and center of the collective response. Its presence reinforces the discipline of nearby Simbakubs, making coordinate

label: sivatherium
description: Sivatherium are imposing herbivores of Earth's ancient megafauna, colossi of muscle and bone marked by thick necks and branching horns like bony crowns. Roaming open plains and forest edges, they command respect even among large predators.\n\nAlthough generally peaceful, threatened adults can become living walls of bone and muscle. Their carcasses yield large amounts of megabone, and their horns a

label: Sporemole
attackSummary: gnawing bite(12p/1.6s); crushing bite(18p/2.5s); head slam(10p/2.0s)
description: Sporemoles are monstrous descendants of ancient burrowing moles, deformed by their parasitic relationship with the Mycorgloom fungus. Their bodies serve as living soil for glowing fungal growths, making them larger, tougher and far harder to kill than any ordinary subterranean animal.\n\nOnce insect-eaters, they became opportunistic carnivores. They ambush prey from tunnels, defend burrows brutall

label: worhin
description: Worhins are colossal beasts of the glacial plains, clad in golden-gray wool and carried by bodies heavy enough to cross snow, ice and open ground without hesitation. From a distance they seem like great herd herbivores; up close, they are living walls of muscle, wool and horn.\n\nIn the present, colonies that manage to domesticate them use Worhins as heavy pack animals and beasts of war. Their siz

label: bigfoot
attackSummary: left fist(18p/2s); right fist(18p/2s); Bite(22p/2.5s); head(17p/2s)
description: Standing at roughly 8-9 feet tall, and with it's characteristic feet measuring up to 24 inches long, Bigfoot is a towering ape-like creature that inhabits the deep forests. Being a very solitary and shy creature, Bigfoot sightings are usually exremely rare as they often flee from humans and avoid being seen. \n\nBigfoots are incredibly intelligent creatures, and are known to build temporary shelte

label: giant
attackSummary: left fist(36p/4s); right fist(36p/4s); Bite(25p/3.5s); head(32p/5s)
description:
Massive, exraordinarily dangerous humanoids, Giants are feared all across the land due to their extreme strength and might. These creatures can easily destroy entire villages, sweeping people and obstacles out of the way with their gargantuan arms. 

Their diet may consist of people, livestock, or local wildlife. For fun, they enjoy wrestling thrumbos or throwing innocent people's houses. 

Yo

label: gnome
attackSummary: left fist(3.6p/1.5s); right fist(3.6p/1.5s); Bite(4p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: Stout humanoid creatures that typically live underground. They are sometimes also referred to as "mountain spirits" because of their preference for living underground. Gnomes are known for both helping and harming miners, either by rewarding them with rich veins of ore, or collapsing mines and throwing rocks at miners. \n\nGnomes will periodically reward humans that are kind to them with silver.

label: goblin
attackSummary: left fist(3.6p/1.5s); right fist(3.6p/1.5s); Bite(4p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: A small, disgusting green humanoid creature of European folklore. Goblins can range from being simply mischievous to outright evil and malicious. Nevertheless, goblins are usually not to be trusted by humans due to their nature. \n\nThough lone goblins are easily dispatched, their large numbers make them a formidable threat.

label: goblin warrior
attackSummary: left fist(4.6p/1.5s); right fist(4.6p/1.5s); Bite(6p/2s); head(3p/2s)
description: A small, disgusting green humanoid creature of European folklore. Goblins can range from being simply mischievous to outright evil and malicious. Nevertheless, goblins are usually not to be trusted by humans due to their nature. \n\nThough lone goblins are easily dispatched, their large numbers make them a formidable threat.

label: imp
attackSummary: left fist(3.6p/1.5s); right fist(3.6p/1.5s); Bite(4p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: Derived from ancient European mythology, the imp is a small, mischievous creature that enjoys pranking and misleading humans for fun. Despite this, imps are mostly harmless and are more of an annoyance than anything. \n\nThough they are wild and unpredictable, imps can be tamed and can make for useful servants.

label: leprechaun
attackSummary: left fist(3.6p/1.5s); right fist(3.6p/1.5s); Bite(4p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: Leprechauns are supernatural beings in Irish folklore commonly depicted as short-framed green-wearing shoemakers. They are often seen running about in forests and gardens. \n\nLeprechauns are known to possess massive amounts of wealth in gold. When tamed, they can be periodically "sheared" for their gold. However, they refuse to tell you where their true fortune lies.

label: skeleton
attackSummary: left fist(3.6p/1.5s); right fist(3.6p/1.5s); Bite(4p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: An undead skeleton, reanimated by an unknown force. It roams the region for an unknown purpose.

label: slime
description: Simple gelatinous creatures that roam the world across many biomes.

label: troll
attackSummary: left fist(16p/2s); right fist(16p/2s); Bite(19p/2.5s); head(15p/2s)
description: Trolls are large, simple-minded humanoids that live together in caves and mountains. Trolls are extremely strong and aggressive, and they usually live far off the beaten path away from civilization.\n\nMany adventurers are warned of the dangers of passing through a troll's territory.

label: unicorn
attackSummary: horn(18p/2s); head(10p/2.9s); left hoof(7p/2s); right hoof(7p/2s); Bite(5p/2s)
description: A large white horse with a single spiraling horn on it's head. It is sometimes thought to have magical abilities, and is far more difficult to tame than a regular horse. It's horn fetches a high price.

label: alligator
attackSummary: left claw(12p/2s); right claw(12p/2s); Bite(22p/2.6s); head(8p/2s)
description: A large semi-aquatic reptile with a powerful bite. Alligators are slow on land, but deadly in the water.

label: alpha thrumbo
attackSummary: horn(34p/2s); Bite(42p/2.6s); left foot(28p/2.6s); right foot(28p/2.6s); head(26p/2s)
description: A gigantic, graceful creature of unknown origin. Alpha thrumbos are even rarer and more dangerous than the typical thrumbo. Their hide is nearly impossible to pierce and their razor-sharp horn is worth more than its weight in gold.\n\nAlpha thrumbos are some of the longest-lived moving creatures in the known universe. Some tribes believe they remember and psychically pass on everything they ever e

label: badger
attackSummary: left claw(4p/1.5s); right claw(4p/1.5s); Bite(7p/2s); head(3p/2s)
description: A stocky omnivorous mammal. Badgers are surprisingly tough for their size.

label: bluebird
description: A small songbird with vibrant blue plumage.

label: bog hound
attackSummary: left claw(10.5p/2s); right claw(10.5p/2s); Bite(17p/2.6s); head(6p/2s)
description: Descended from domesticated dogs, these canines have grown unaccustomed to human company. They're skilled scavengers, able to survive in extremely toxic environments. Bog hounds are harder to tame than their domesticated cousins, and much more dangerous.

label: bullfrog
description: A large frog known for its loud croak. Bullfrog legs are a delicacy on some planets.

label: scimitar cat
attackSummary: left claw(11p/1.5s); right claw(11p/1.5s); Bite(16p/2s); head(9p/2s)
description: A bioengineered predator that resembles its long-extinct namesake. Originally bred to populate iceworld hunting reserves, these animals are now common pets among glitterworld socialites. Their ferocity should not be underestimated.

label: colossus toad
description: A massive frog bioengineered for industrial farms. While safe to eat, its thick skin secretes an unpleasant slime.

label: crow
description: Intelligent black birds with complex social structures. With a little patience, crows can be trained to perform a number of fairly complex tasks.

label: hunter drone
description: An automated kill drone. The hunter drone pursues its target and detonates when it gets close.

label: sentry drone
description: An automated security drone. It continuously patrols an area, looking for intruders. Once an intruder is found, it will relentlessly attack with a short-range scattergun. Its long-lasting battery can keep it going for centuries.

label: wasp
description: A small drone used for defense and situation control. The drone injects a small amount of paralytic biotoxin, stunning organic targets. While designed to be non-lethal, wasps may occasionally kill their target by accident. Wasps are powered by a long-lasting battery.

label: flamingo
description: A wading bird known for their vibrant pink plumage. Their long legs are well adapted to shallow waters.

label: gorilla
attackSummary: left fist(14p/1.5s); right fist(14p/1.5s); Bite(10p/2s); head(6p/2s)
description: A massive and intelligent great ape. While generally peaceful, gorillas are terrifying when enraged.

label: hermit crab
description: A small crustacean found along coastlines. Hermit crabs scavenge various shells to protect themselves.

label: heron
description: Long-legged and long-necked birds. They tend to live in marshy habitats.

label: hippo
description: An enormous semi-aquatic mammal with short stocky legs. While it is a herbivore, it can attack with devastating force if provoked. Its powerful jaw can crush bone and armor.

label: hive queen
description: The birth mother of an insect megahive. Under suitable conditions, several distinct insect hives will merge together and produce a hive queen. The queen quickly grows in size, becoming trapped in her own burrow.

label: larva
description: The juvenile form of larger bioengineered insects. Larva maintain and expand hives using an acidic secretion. If provoked, they defend themselves by spewing sludge.

label: lava snail
description: A large slow-moving mollusk. Originating from the volcanic planet Nuchadus, lava snails were bred as farm animals. Their skin secretes a thick slime that protects them from extreme temperatures.

label: locust
description: A bioengineered insect capable of flying short distances. Specialized chemical receptors allow locusts to effectively forage for food. While relatively weak on their own, swarms of locusts can be deadly.

label: macaw
description: A parrot known for its intelligence and its brilliant plumage.

label: mastodon
attackSummary: tusk(27.5p/2.6s); left foot(18.6p/2s); right foot(18.6p/2s); head(15.5p/2s)
description: A massive elephant-like mammal. While briefly extinct, the mastodon now roams countless worlds due to its resilience to bitter cold. Its thick hide makes excellent cold-weather clothing. However, hunting the animal is a dangerous proposition even for skilled hunters.

label: cyclops
attackSummary: front left leg(12.0p/2s); front right leg(12.0p/2s); head(8.5p/2s)
description: A front-line combat mechanoid named for its large optical array. The cyclops specializes in counter-shield attacks. It takes a long time to lock onto a target, but once locked on, it fires a near endless barrage of shield-piercing beams.

label: megavole
attackSummary: left claw(8p/2s); right claw(8p/2s); Bite(14p/2.6s); head(5p/2s)
description: A massive burrowing rodent, bred for its size and strength. It's almost completely blind but can be surprisingly aggressive when cornered. On some low-tech worlds, these creatures are trained to dig for valuable minerals.

label: mink
attackSummary: left claw(3p/2s); right claw(3p/2s); Bite(6p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: A small semi-aquatic mammal. The high value of its fur has resulted in mink being farmed on numerous planets.

label: monitor lizard
attackSummary: left claw(8p/2s); right claw(8p/2s); ToxicBite(12p/2.6s); head(5p/2s)
description: A large venomous lizard. They secrete toxins from venom glands in their lower jaw to neutralize their prey.

label: moose
attackSummary: left hoof(12p/2s); right hoof(12p/2s); Bite(12p/2s); head(15.5p/2.6s)
description: One of the largest members of the deer family, adapted to extremely cold climates. Its long legs allow it to travel easily through deep snow.

label: muskox
attackSummary: left hoof(10p/2s); right hoof(10p/2s); Bite(10p/2s); head(14p/2.6s)
description: A shaggy hoofed mammal found in colder climates. Muskox wool is known for being scratchy, but offers good protection against the cold.

label: otter
attackSummary: left claw(3.6p/1.5s); right claw(3.6p/1.5s); Bite(6p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: A playful marine creature. They use tools such as rocks to crack open shellfish.

label: panda
attackSummary: left claw(10p/2s); right claw(10p/2s); Bite(12p/2.6s); head(6p/2s)
description: A slow lumbering herbivore. Pandas are admired by many for their clumsy charm, making them common pets on urbworlds. On the rim, pandas are rarely seen outside of captivity.

label: peafowl
description: Large birds with extravagant plumage. Male peacocks use their tail feathers in elaborate courtship displays.

label: porcupine
attackSummary: left claw(3.6p/1.5s); right claw(3.6p/1.5s); PorcupineBite(6p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: A large rodent. While slow moving, it has a cloak of sharp quills which protect it from predators.

label: prairie dog
attackSummary: left claw(3.6p/1.5s); right claw(3.6p/1.5s); Bite(6p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: A burrowing rodent with a short tail and sharp claws used for digging. They are social animals, often living in large colonies.

label: quail
description: Small plump ground-dwelling birds with a distinctive plume.

label: sea lion
description: A large and intelligent marine animal. Male sea lions have thick fur around their necks, which evoke a lion's mane.

label: sea turtle
description: A large marine turtle. Their streamlined shell and powerful flippers make them excellent swimmers.

label: seal
description: A marine mammal with a streamlined body that is adept at hunting fish. While slow on land, seals are relatively quick in water.

label: sparrow
description: Small birds that often travel in flocks. They can thrive in a variety of environments.

label: stone crab
description: A robust crustacean with powerful claws. Stone crabs are a delicacy in some regions.

label: swan
description: Large graceful waterfowl known for their beauty, and their surprising ferocity.

label: tiger
attackSummary: left claw(11p/1.5s); right claw(11p/1.5s); Bite(16p/2s); head(9p/2s)
description: A solitary and dangerous apex predator. Tigers make quick work of their prey, using a mix of stealth and razor-sharp claws.

label: vulture
description: Scavengers with strong beaks and broad wings. Their strong stomach acid allows them to eat rotting corpses.

label: walrus
description: A large marine animal with tusks and whiskers. Its considerable bulk allows it to survive in extremely cold environments. While slow on land, it is relatively quick in water.

label: greatwolf
attackSummary: left claw(10.9p/2s); right claw(10.9p/2s); Bite(12p/2s); head(6p/2s)
description: A genetically engineered canine modeled on long-extinct dire wolves. These fearsome predators were created as pets for the glitterworld elite. Wild greatwolves now populate many planets, due to their tendency to escape confinement.

label: wolverine
attackSummary: left claw(9p/2s); right claw(9p/2s); Bite(10p/2s); head(4p/2s)
description: A small but ferocious predator. Wolverines are solitary animals that prefer to eat carrion but can kill animals many times their size if needed.

label: Astromech Droid
description: An astromech, smart and robust droids, particularly good at hacking and research.

label: DUM Repair Droid
description: A DUM-series pit droid, a model of repair droid manufactured by Serv-O-Droid Inc. They are a common sight in salvage yards, despite their intended design of maintaining podracers, they are cheap and expendable enough that many others have taken them on as a form of general purpose droid.

label: Destroyer Droid
description: Manufactured by the Colicoids on Colla IV, droidekas were dangerous and deadly, designed to exterminate their adversaries with extreme prejudice.

label: fx-7 medical droid
description: An fx-7 medical droid, capable of performing medical procedures.

label: GNK Power Droid
description: An GNK Power Droid, simply functions as a moving power generator, filling batteries it's close to.

label: MSE Repair Droid
description: An MSE Repair Droid, repairs other droids within a 2 tile radius and is capable of hauling and cleaning.

label: Muckraker Crab Droid
description: The LM-432 "Muckraker" crab droid, commonly referred to as the crab droid or simply "Muckraker," was a four-legged droid walker of various sizes manufactured by the Techno Union. These droids are the equivalent of a small tank with the firepower they typically carried, however they are surprisingly useful at mining.

label: salvage assist droid
description: A groundmech salvage assist droid, cheap to produce but not capable of much beyond hauling and cleaning.

label: flatworm hound
description: One of the simplest giant microbes to develop in the primordial fields. Remarkably, it has been modified to be quite docile, tameable, can eat just about anything, and requires very little food. These flatworms can grow accustomed to people, and have even been genetically modified to nuzzle, and their odd squishy texture is surprisingly nice to pet. Though their brains are so small, it is doubtful

label: hydrazoa
description: An incredibly aggressive, simple minded hunter. It's tiny brain can only handle one thought, hunger.

label: jellybird
description: A small floating jellyfish-like creature that hovers above the ground. They have a painful sting, and travel in flocks over the primordial geysers.

label: giant tardigrade
attackSummary: head(10p/2.9s); Bite(15p/2s); left claw(12p/1.8s); right claw(12p/1.8s)
description: A spectacularly large version of the normally microscopic creature. It is large, docile, can carry caravan goods, and can be milked for microbe squeezins.

label: chaos chicken
description: This bizarre purple chicken, presumably made by some mad Archotech, lays eggs which, when fertilized by an ordinary rooster, can hatch into seemingly any species of animal at complete random.\n\nAll attempts at removing its hat have resulted in the death of at least 20 humanoids.

label: hemolope
attackSummary: head(5p/2s); left hoof(7p/2s); right hoof(7p/2s); Bite(8p/2s)
description: Engineered for hemogen production, the hemolope grows a large sac of pure hemogen on its back. Due to genetic instabilities, unlike a boomalope, it has a very short lifespan and is generally weaker. It has rarely been encountered in the wild, as it is only kept by more ethical sanguophages for corporations for hemogen production. It can be milked to produce hemogen.

label: kiwi
description: The miniscule, spherical cousin of the moa. Inferior in every way to their bigger relative. Helpless in the face of danger because of it's lack of flight.

label: neutrolope
attackSummary: head(7p/2s); left hoof(9p/2s); right hoof(9p/2s); Bite(10p/2s)
description: Engineered for neutroamine production, the neutrolope grows a large sac of pure neutroamine on its back. Though it is weak and fragile for its size, other animals avoid it similarly to a boomalope, despite the fact it does not explode when it dies. It can be milked to produce neutroamine.

label: rabbit
description: This small and fluffy, solitary herbivore can swiftly hop away from danger.

label: rimclaw
attackSummary: horn(15p/2s); left claw(32p/1.5s); right claw(32p/1.5s); Bite(25p/2.5s); head(15p/1.95s)
description: Rimclaws are giant apex predators mutated from iguana, well adapted to highly polluted environments. They are incredibly fast, powerful and intelligent.

label: woolly stegosaurus
attackSummary: head(14p/2.5s); Bite(12p/2s); left foot(8p/5s); right foot(8p/5s); tail spikes(32p/2.2s)
description: A variation of the more common “roof lizard”, this creature is a herbivore characterized by their distinctive kite-shaped upright bony scales along the back which help regulate their body temperature and acts as a mating display.\n\nThe Woolly Stegosaurus finds their home in cold biomes, preferring to eat low-lying vegetation due to a short neck and small head. The spines on the end of the tail di

label: owlbeast
attackSummary: left claw(17p/2s); right claw(17p/2s); beak(23.6p/2.6s); head(11p/2s)
description: A huge omnivorous genetically engineered mammal adapted for temperate climates, having been created by combining the DNA of a common grizzly bear and owl. It is nocturnal in nature and has wings on its back that are too small for it to support body weight for flight. \n\nWhile their usual diet consists of fish, berries, honey, and scavenged meat, the owlbeast is capable of using its massive streng

label: 巨型蟑螂
description: 一种来自旧世界的人造昆虫,拥有着和蟑螂相似的外观,但成虫的长度却能够达到整整2米,是人们生活中亲切的朋友.经过训练的能够帮助人类幼崽在上下学的时候避开机动车,在低空飞驰;但这种昆虫由于基因中被抹除了和战斗相关的基因,虽然有着足以一口撕裂成年男性人类的口器和坚固的甲壳,因此它们几乎没有任何攻击欲望,并不适合用于战斗.\n由于特殊的基因编辑,这种巨型昆虫在经过培训后,能够自发的寻找垃圾并吞噬,通过特殊的消化系统转化为虫胶,虽然很多人无法接受这种垃圾所转化的虫胶,但这种虫胶确实和其他天然昆虫所分泌的并无区别.

label: 机械蟑螂
description: 一只蟑螂形态的机械,但大小显然并不正常,这只2人大的机械蟑螂有着锋利的口器和弹射装置,可以从中等距离扑到敌人的脸上并剪断他们的脖子,杀伤力极其恐怖,且厚重的装甲赋予了其极强的的生存能力,能够在枪林弹雨中穿梭如风

label: skunk
description: A small omnivorous mammal best known for its ability to spray a liquid with a foul odor from its anal glands when threatened.

label: Space Worm
description: An extra-terrestrial parasite, the Space Worm has been given its nickname by Colonists across the Rimworlds for the way in which it slithers towards its prey. Once a parasite has successfully infected its prey, the prey (host) will undergo a series of symptoms from nausea to unconciousness. After 24 hours, infant Space Worms will hatch from the host, killing them in the process.

label: acklay
description: The acklay is a non-sentient carnivore native to planet Vendaxa. Acklays have sharp claws, thick skin, and are about 3 meters tall. Due to these attributes, as well as the species' ferocity, acklays are often exported from Vendaxa to be used in gladiatorial combat. The creatures can be found on Geonosis, where they are commonly brought in to fight other creatures—and sentients—in the Petranaki are

label: aiwha
description: Aiwhas could be found on several worlds where they lived in medium-size "pods," feeding on fish and other small creatures found in or around huge bodies of water. Aiwhas are sometimes sold so as to be used as mounts on worlds that have a breathable atmosphere, and could be used for performing reconnaissance, or to traverse between two outposts without any concern for the trail or terrain.

label: akk
description: Akk (or sometimes called 'akk hounds'), were large reptomammals native to the planet Haruun Kal. Great companions, Akk matured from pups to hounds in a relatively short time and were often used for protection due to their likelihood to form strong bonds with their master. The illegal smuggling of these loyal but dangerous creatures has lead to them being found on many worlds.

label: anooba
attackSummary: left paw(10.9p/2s); right paw(10.9p/2s); Bite(16p/2s); head(6p/2s)
description: Anoobas were aggressive pack predators that lived throughout the Outer Rim Territories. Opportunistic hunters as well as scavengers, these wolflike canines would attack virtually anything smaller than themselves (such as scurriers).

label: bantha
attackSummary: horns(23p/2.4s); horns(23p/2.4s); head(13p/2.6s); left hoof(10p/2s); right hoof(10p/2s); Bite(10p/2s)
description: Banthas are a species of large, hairy mammals with sharp, spiraling horns. They inhabit the desert planet Tatooine, though they are bred on many worlds throughout the galaxy. They are social herd animals, and are often domesticated, and used prominently, by Tusken Raiders as mounts and companionship.

label: behemoth
attackSummary: tusk(28p/2s); left foot(19p/2s); right foot(19p/2s); head(19p/2s)
description: The Behemoths (or 'Sith war behemoths') were beasts of war used by the Sith that originated from the frozen planet Khar Dhelba. Wild war behemoths tended to travel in small groups of two to four and spent most of their existence searching for food. They were omnivorous in the sense that they ate anything they were able to find. The Behemoths were spread to various worlds with the Sith armies, eith

label: beldon
description: Beldons were a large cnidaria species native to the gas giant Bespin. They lived in the planet's lower atmosphere and could be found in large herds. They used the long tendrils on their bodies to gather atmospheric plankton and chemicals and so require very little direct nutrition. This variety appears to have been engineered to not only survive away from Bespin, but create useful Chemfuel and are

label: blarth
attackSummary: left paw(3.6p/2s); right paw(3.6p/2s); cute teeth(5.8p/2s); head(4p/2s)
description: Blarths were medium-sized predators native to the planet Naboo named for the low burping sound that it made. Amiable and easily tamed, they were kept as a household pet and watch animal by Gungans since prehistoric times. More recently the animals had made their way to off-world pet shops on worlds such as Coruscant.

label: blixus
attackSummary: left tentacle(18p/2s); central tentacle(18p/2s); right tentacle(18p/2s); Bite(24p/2.6s)
description: Blixus were rare, half-shelled crustapod creatures native to the planet Sljee. These semi-aquatic predators were known to be deadly in the swamps and lagoons they inhabit. They were known to periodically shed their exoskeleton if broken or damaged which could be harvested for useful chitin. It is believed many were accidently transplanted to various worlds as exotic display animals or pets that gr

label: blurrg
attackSummary: left claws(3.6p/2s); right claws(3.6p/2s); Bite(19p/2s); head(15p/2s)
description: Blurrgs were a two-legged non-sentient reptilian species that were used as beasts of burden on a number of worlds located across the galaxy. Blurrgs had two short arms that had two fingers with claws, and a thick tail that helped them balance. The creatures possessed large mouths and many sharp teeth that could chew through most materials, including grasses and weeds, though they were not strictly

label: Boar-wolf
attackSummary: left paw(12p/2s); right paw(12p/2s); Bite(18p/2s); head(6p/2s)
description: The boar-wolves (or 'Borra'), were a predatory animal that came from the forest moon of Endor. Boar-wolves were believed to be closer to wolves than boars physiologically speaking, and usually hunted for prey such as blurrgs. They could be trained as attack beasts and so have been exported to various worlds by criminal elements for such purposes.

label: bogwing
attackSummary: left clawed paw(8p/1.5s); right clawed paw(8p/1.5s); beak(12p/2s); head(6p/1.5s)
description: The bogwing is a fast flying reptavian native to Dagobah. They could be found on a number of worlds located across the galaxy. They mostly fed on small creatures dwelling in the lower levels of tree canopies (including rodents like leaftails) to avoid larger predators.

label: bolotaur
description: The Bolotaur are a large, long-necked herbivorous reptilian creatures native to the planet Kashyyyk. They were short-lived but reproduced quickly and were a favoured mount by the Trandoshan species, which resulted in their spread to many worlds as beasts of burden and livestock.

label: boma
description: Bomas were ravenous beasts native to planet Onderon and its moon Dxun. In their native environment they hunted Cannoks with ease and were considered dangerous by several Mandalorian clans. They were sometimes introduced into ecosystems on other worlds where Cannoks had become established to help maintain their population.

label: Borcatu
attackSummary: left claw(6p/2s); right claw(6p/2s); PorcupineBite(6p/2s); head(6p/2s)
description: Borcatu were small, bad-tempered scavengers originally found on the planet of Escabar. Borcatu had a scaly, thick hide which may have evolved to help resist sandstorms. They also have sharp teeth, claws and quills to defend themselves. They had a vicious temperament, biting anyone who came near them, and often fighting and cannibalizing one another when no other food source was available. Their ha

label: bordok
attackSummary: head(12p/2.9s); left hoof(8p/2s); right hoof(8p/2s); horn(6p/2s)
description: The bordoks were a vaguely equine herbivore native to the forest moon of Endor. They were used on many worlds as pack animals when tamed. Bordoks were very sure-footed and, in spite of their size, capable of carrying large loads.

label: brezak
description: Brezaks (also known as "Zygerrian gliding lizards"), were large carnivorous reptavians from the planet Zygerria. Their flat tail served as a rudder, and when controlled by a skilled rider, they were quite agile while in flight. Due to their prevalence within Zyggerian culture, these creatures were transplanted and established themselves on other worlds.

label: bursa
attackSummary: left claw(14p/2s); right claw(14p/2s); Bite(26p/2.6s); head(12p/2s)
description: Bursas were a species of ursidae creatures native to planet of Naboo. They had tusked snouts and feathery tufts of brown hair on their thick-skinned bodies. They were popular as circus animals due to their intelligence, but more often than not this resulted in them escaping and forming wild populations on various temperate worlds.

label: can-cell
description: Can-cells were a species of scavenging flying insectoids found on a number of planets across the galaxy (although it is believed they originated on Kashyyk). Can-Cells evolved many of their strange physical characteristics to maximise their survival in the dangerous forests and jungles they inhabit.

label: cannok
attackSummary: left tridactyl claw(7.2p/2s); right tridactyl claw(7.2p/2s); Bite(9.7p/2s); head(5p/2s)
description: Cannoks were small, aggressive predators native to the moon of Dxun. They had a habit of eating anything that could fit in their mouths and were known as pests, due to a high reproduction rate and notable curiosity. Cannoks were however hardy and able to survive the rigors of many worlds.

label: chrysalide rancor
attackSummary: left hand(30p/2s); right hand(30p/2s); teeth(40p/2s); left foot(18p/2s); right foot(18p/2s); head(20p/2s)
description: The chrysalide (also known as the "chrysalis beast" or "chrysalide rancor"), was a creature created from rancors and altered by Sith alchemy. It was widely believed that during ancient times, the knowledge of creating the chrysalis beast was formed by the ancient Sith race. In those early years, the creatures served the Sith Empire as pets or protectors to high-ranking officers or powerful nobles.

label: clodhopper
attackSummary: left foot(6p/2s); right foot(6p/2s); Bite(5p/2.6s); head(4p/2s)
description: Clodhoppers were omnivorous and dim-witted flightless avians from the planet Naboo but could be found as castaway populations on numerous worlds due to illegal egg exports. Clodhopper weren't large creatures, but they fed in swarms becoming a real menace to agriculture. They were protected by tough, durable skin. Fast-breeding, dimwitted, voracious grazers, clodhoppers would use their powerful for

label: convor
description: Convor (also known as "Trandoshan birds"), were a species of beautiful mammavian from the Wasskah moon of Hsskhor. Although Convor had short, plump bodies, they were excellent fliers. Their popularity as a pet meant they often established colonies on other worlds.

label: corellian hound
attackSummary: left claw(8.9p/2s); right claw(8.9p/2s); Bite(14p/2s); head(6p/2s)
description: Corellian hounds, also known as 'Sibian hounds' or 'Snarlers', were a type of stout canidae from the planet Corellia. They were quick and nimble canines used by locals for a number of tasks although they were often used for hunting and tracking. They had a vicious bark and bite, which meant they could be quite effective for protection.

label: corinathoth
description: Corinathoths were large, slow-moving herbivores native to the planet Maridun. Although large and intimidating, they were fairly harmless unless provoked. It is likely they were spread as a large game animal to several worlds due to their fearsome appearance.

label: dactillion
description: The dactillions were a reptavian native to the sinkhole world of Utapau. Dactillions shared both avian and lizard traits, with long, thin wings and thick, scaled hides. A dactillion's pair of wings allowed it to ride the thermal updrafts in a Utapau sinkhole, and its prominent limbs allowed it to scale the rocky side. An avian cousin of the speedy varactyl, the dactillion served as a mounts.

label: dalgo
attackSummary: head(10p/2.9s); left hoof(8p/2s); right hoof(8p/2s); Bite(8p/2s)
description: Dalgos were equine reptiles native to the planet of Onderon. Despite being carnivorous predators, they could still be domesticated and filled the same role as other beasts of burden. It is for this reason these creatures found themselves spread across many worlds.

label: devourer
attackSummary: left fist(18p/1.5s); right fist(18p/1.5s); Bite(20p/2s); head(8p/2s)
description: Devourers were carnivorous anthropoids twisted by the dark side of the Force that were indigenous to jungle moon of Dxun. Devourers were known across many worlds for having attacked (and in some instances killed) several notable figures in galactic history who wandered into their territory. They were fierce creatures and were sometimes exported as attack animals to other worlds where escaped speci

label: dewback
description: Dewbacks are large, four-legged, omnivorous, cold-blooded reptiles native to the Dune Sea of Tatooine. As such, they are well-adapted to the harsh desert climate. This and the fact that they can be easily domesticated make them commonly employed as beasts of burden by both the inhabitants of the desert planet and the off-worlders wandering its dunes. Due to their numerous useful traits and versati

label: dianoga
description: Dianoga originated on the planet Vodran and were large cephalopods capable of growing to great sizes. They had a single eyestalk protruding from their mollusk-like bodies, and seven suckered tentacles surrounding a fanged maw containing a sharp serrated probe. Normally these creatures were restricted to bodies of water, but this variety seems just as comfortable dragging itself around on land.

label: Dragonsnake
description: The dragonsnake (also spelled 'dragon snake') were a large, semi-aquatic predatory reptiles that dwelled in the muddy waters of various planets, including Dagobah and Nal Hutta. Dragonsnakes were large serpentlike beasts with sharp fangs and biolumescent spots along their backs. Although voracious, they were incapable of digesting metal (a lucky escape for some heroic droids!). The dragonsnake "Br

label: drexl
attackSummary: left claws(20p/1.5s); right claws(20p/1.5s); Bite(26p/2s); serated tail(18p/2.2s); horned head(14p/2s)
description: Drexls (also known as 'warbeasts') were reptavian winged creatures indigenous to Onderonian moon of Dxun. In early stages of Onderon history, drexls were feared predators that spread terror, attacking the primitive Onderonian villages. The creatures were later trained as mounts by the Onderonian outcasts, who came to be known as 'Beast Riders'. Their viciousness as 'warbeasts' resulted in them bei

label: energy spider
description: Energy spiders (or "spice spiders") were horrifying arachnids that inhabited the Spice Mines of Kessel. The webs that these creatures spin between their legs can be harvested as Glitterstim (a potent drug and medicinal ingredient). This variety of Energy Spider appears to have been bioengineered to survive off of Kessel but with the downside that they have massive appetites. They can however survi

label: eopie
attackSummary: head(12p/2.9s); left hoof(8p/2s); right hoof(8p/2s); Bite(6p/2s)
description: Eopies were a species of quadrupedal mammallian herbivores native to the planet Tatooine. These tough creatures were acclimated to their homeworld's endless deserts, and as a result were domesticated and exported offworld as pack animals. The eopie's rough skin helped to protect it against the heat while its hooves were adapted to climbing rocky cliffs.

label: falumpaset
attackSummary: head(14p/2.9s); left hoof(12p/2s); right hoof(12p/2s); Bite(18p/2s)
description: The falumpaset were a large mammalalian creature native to the planet Naboo. Their distinctive bellowing calls could be heard for kilometers around and their intelligence made them likely to form strong bonds with their handlers. Easily domesticated as beasts of burden (or sometimes war mounts), falumpasets could be found all over the galaxy.

label: fambaa
attackSummary: Bite(28p/2.6s); left foot(19p/2s); right foot(19p/2s); head(17p/2s)
description: Fambaas were large herbivorous amphibians most often found in swamps. Fambaas were technically amphibians but had the scaly hide of reptiles. The creatures size and usefulness when domesticated meant they were exported to many worlds as beasts of burden.

label: fanback
attackSummary: tusk(14p/2s); tail(8p/2.2s); left claw(8p/1.5s); right claw(8p/1.5s)
description: The fanback was a cold-blooded predatory amphibian from the swamps of Naboo. Each fanback had a big dorsal spine along with a sensitive snout which allowed them to hunt for fish and other small free swimming prey with ease. They lay a high number of eggs and were known to protect these nest sites by hunting any creature bold enough to attempt to eat or threaten their clutch. It's for this reason t

label: feral grazer
description: These slow-moving herbivorous mammalia were native to Alderaan. 'Feral' or 'wild' grazers were significantly leaner than the fatter and more well-fed domestic grazer; however both species were distantly related to Nerfs. Their horns, tough leathery hides and fat layers acted as an additional defense against predation.

label: feral nerf
attackSummary: horns(10p/1.65s); left hoof(10p/2s); right hoof(10p/2s); Bite(10p/2s); head(13p/2.6s)
description: Nerfs were a species of antlered, herbivorous mammalia found all across the galaxy. Because of the nerf's ability to easily adapt to harsh environments, several defined sub-species existed and were often referred to as 'feral' or 'wild' variants of the same animal.

label: frilled gorg
description: Frilled Gorgs, were small frilled amphibians that could be found on several planets. This subspecies was notable for the frills along it's back and tail (hence the name) and for being slightly more aggressive in nature. Their spread to others worlds is often the consequence of culinary import of either eggs or escaped live specimens.

label: frog dog
description: Frog dogs (sometimes referred to as "frog-dogs" or "frogdogs") were a species of reptillians with both frog-like and dog-like features. The creatures hopped and waddled from place to place. Frog-dog vocalizations sounded like throaty barks and croaks. This variant was popular on planets such as At Attin due to their bright, inquisitive, loyal, and attentive nature. "At Attin frogdogs" were sought

label: gelagrub
description: Gelagrubs, also known as 'Felucian ground beetles', were large insectine creatures native to Felucia. This variety (with some genetic tweaking) found themselves popular for export to many Rimworlds because they remained in their useful grub-like state for their entire lives whilst also swapping out their normal phosphorescence for neutroamine production.

label: gizka
attackSummary: left foot(2p/2s); right foot(2p/2s); Bite(4p/2.6s); head(3p/2s)
description: Whatever their native world, their extraordinary reproduction rate led to a fair amount of gizka on many worlds, even including uncharted planets such as Lehon, finding their way from the wreckage of crashed starships. It has been alternatively postulated that they came from that planet originally, spreading along with the Infinite Empire. Their exponential population growth led to them being cons

label: gorg
description: Gorgs, known as 'chubas' in Huttese, were small precocious amphibians that could be found on several planets. They were popularly favored as food by many humanoid species. Thus they became popular livestock on sparse worlds due to their high temperature tolerance, minimal food consumption and fast breeding.

label: gornt
description: The gornt was a domesticated, omnivorous creature native on the world of Hethar. A naturally bred gornt would grow to a meter or more long and was supported by four limbs, two small front legs and two large hind legs. Their head had a single horn and their mouths were surrounded by tendrils which they used to eat almost anything. It was introduced to many worlds as their meat was found to be sweet

label: granite slug
description: The granite slug was a silica parasite native to the planet Coruscant. This small terrestrial mollusk has corrosive acidic green-gray slime blood. Its body consisted of four eyestalks, two retractable mouths, one foot, lung filaments, and suction pseudopods. One of their natural predators is the hawk-bat.

label: Grank
attackSummary: left claw(10p/2s); right claw(10p/2s); Bite(16p/2s); head(6p/2s)
description: The Grank (or 'saw-toothed grank') were a medium-sized carnivore believed to have originated on the planet Naboo. They were a species of predatory scavengers with sharp teeth and powerful jaws. Despite their fearsome gnarled appearance they were very affectionate when domesticated. This made them popular pets and lead to them establishing wild populations on multiple worlds as a result.

label: grazer
description: A large, slow domesticated mammalia from Alderaan that has been selectively bred to produce huge amounts of milk. Their fat reserves function to insulate them well against a broad range of temperature. However, most of them are so adapted to farm life that they cannot survive in the wild like their feral brethren.

label: greater krayt dragon
attackSummary: front left leg(35p/2s); front right leg(35p/2s); teeth(45p/2s); Tail(45p/3s); head(35p/2s)
description: The greater krayt dragon was the largest species of krayt dragon, and the apex predator of the planet Tatooine. Using its ten strong legs, it literally swam through the shifting sands. This larger subspecies is both rarer and yet it was still hunted (some say foolishly as most hunts end in disaster) for the precious pearls found in their bodies and as a right of passage for certain Tusken tribes.

label: gualaar
attackSummary: horn(20p/2s); left hoof(15p/2s); right hoof(15p/2s); Bite(18p/2s)
description: The Gualaar was an ungulate species indigenous to the mountains and hills of the planet Naboo. These creatures though tricky to domesticate had both the build and strength to make them perfect beasts of burden. The Royal House of Naboo kept a herd of Gualaar that were used to carry state officials. This regal affiliation and their physical practicality meant they were exported and ultimately sprea

label: gullipud
description: Gullipuds were bulky, loose-skinned, self-inflating amphibians native to the swamps of the planet Naboo. As they were small and easy prey for other animals, like pikobis, gullipuds would extend their spine to make themselves harder to catch and swallow. Due to their physical similarities to the more common gorg these creatures may have been unintentionally transported to various worlds as livestoc

label: gundark
attackSummary: left arm(20p/2s); right arm(20p/2s); left middle claw(10p/1s); right middle claw(10p/1s); teeth(26p/2s)
description: Gundarks were fearsome anthropoids from the planet Vanqor. They were known as one of the most vicious, strong, and aggressive species in the galaxy. This ferocity resulted in them being exported across to many worlds as gladiatorial combatants or as exotic pets. They had two powerful arms used in combat and locomotion, two smaller arms for manipulation and walked on a specialised single clawed-toe

label: gutkurr
attackSummary: left sickled claw(13p/1.5s); right sickled claw(13p/1.5s); beaked maw(16p/2s); head(15p/2s)
description: Gutkurrs were fierce insectile predators native to the planet Ryloth. They were aggressive and displayed very limited intelligence, however they were observed to work in small hunting packs. These traits however has made them popular game animals and "pets" for criminal organisations across the galaxy, spreading these monsterous creatures to many worlds.

label: harvester beetle
description: The harvester beetle were a large domesticated insectoid native to the planet Neimoidia, but were transplanted to all the Neimoidian purse worlds (as well as potential) worlds. They were large, herbivorous and were able to carry heavy loads on their swept backs. In the absence of their 'hive queens' pheremones, these animals have become feral but they still make excellent beasts of burden and can

label: hawk-bat
description: Hawk-bats were predatory reptavians with a curved beak and leathery wings that could be found on urbanized worlds like Coruscant and Taris. To get on a hawk-bat's bad side could be very dangerous. As a result, very few lived in captivity. Though they favored granite slugs, hawk-bats would feed on almost anything smaller than themselves. When they hatched from their eggs, young hawk-bats had scaly

label: horax
attackSummary: left foot(22p/1.5s); right foot(22p/1.5s); Bite(25p/2s); head(32p/2s); spiked club-tail(26p/2.4s)
description: Horaxes were colossal, slow reptiles native to the planet Nelvaan. They were capable of growing to huge sizes thanks to the low gravity of their homeworld. Their powerfully muscled frames were covered in thick, knobby, blue skin which provided excellent defence. The mouth of the horax contained many sharp teeth, the most prominent being the four enormous saber-like fangs that protruded from its ma

label: hrumph
attackSummary: left hoof(12p/1.5s); right hoof(12p/1.5s); Bite(14p/2s); head(20p/2s)
description: The hrumphs were powerful, thick-necked herbivores native to planet Naboo, but also found on other worlds like Aargonar. Hrumphs received their name from the loud, deep, guttural sounds they produced. They had four long horns for defense and for the protection of their two long, sensitive ears. They were not choosy about their food which made them hardy enough to survive on many other worlds.

label: hssiss
attackSummary: poisonous fangs(18p/2.6s); tusk(14p/2s); tail(16p/2.2s); left claw(12p/1.5s); right claw(12p/1.5s)
description: Hssiss (or "dark side dragons") were a poisnous reptile native to the planet Ambria. They were slow but aggressive ambush predators that preferred to live near bodies of water. Hssiss could be found all over the galaxy, especially on worlds where the "dark side" was strong (with most being descended from those brought by the many historical "Sith" armies).

label: igitz
attackSummary: left paw(3.0p/2s); right paw(3.0p/2s); fish teeth(4.8p/2s); head(6p/2s)
description: Igitz were a species of small amphibians hailing from the planet Naboo. Those blue-skinned, omnivorous critters dwelled in the planet's many dense swamps. Because of the environment in which they had evolved, the igitz were well-adapted to both land and water: while their front paws were clawed for treading on land, their hindquarters were finned, allowing it speed when in water. The igitz were a

label: insectomorph
attackSummary: teeth(12p/2s); left foot(6p/1.5s); right foot(6p/1.5s); head(10p/2s)
description: Insectomorphs were insectoids from the planet Malastare. These easily domesticated omnivores were often used by the Dugs on their homeworld as battle mounts. Despite their unusual appearance they have been able to flourish as livestock on multiple worlds due to their rapid growth and hardiness.

label: iriaz
attackSummary: left hoof(6p/1.5s); right hoof(6p/1.5s); Bite(6p/2s); head(8p/2s)
description: Iriaz were docile creatures from the grassland planet Dantooine. While not normally aggressive, they could attack if provoked. They were a prey of choice for local hunters (and natural predators alike) given that they were a relatively common creature; furthering their export to many planets.

label: iridonian reek
attackSummary: horn(24p/2s); horn(24p/2s); horn(24p/2s); Bite(15p/2.6s); head(19p/2s); front left hoof(9p/2s); front right hoof(9p/2s)
description: Reek could be found on the planets Iridonia, Kashyyyk, Ithor, Codian Moon, Tatooine and Saleucami (to name just a few). Various subspecies invariably sprung up as the base stock adapted to new environments. The Iridonian Reek was bred as a 'war mount' by the Iridonian Zabraks. Instead of giving them a meat diet, the Iridonian reeks were given a natural diet consisting of plant matter to keep them

label: ithorian reek
attackSummary: horn(15p/2s); horn(15p/2s); horn(15p/2s); Bite(11p/2.6s); head(15p/2s); front left hoof(5p/2s); front right hoof(5p/2s)
description: Reek could be found on the planets Iridonia, Kashyyyk, Ithor, Codian Moon, Tatooine and Saleucami (to name just a few). Various subspecies invariably sprung up as the base stock adapted to new environments. The Ithorian Reek were used as plow animals by the Ithorians and were larger and stronger than those found on Ylesia. Their horns were also smaller because of the lack of hostility between this

label: jakobeast
attackSummary: left tusk(23p/2s); right tusk(23p/2s); horns(13p/2.4s); head(13p/2.6s); left paw(10p/2s); right paw(10p/2s)
description: Jakobeasts were polar herd animals found in the tundras of icy planets in the Outer Rim. Jakobeasts were domesticated primarily for their meat, milk, and fur. While excellent livestock, they were ill-suited to serve as mounts, guards, or attack animals. . Jakobeasts were introduced by colonists that sought herd animals capable of defending themselves. As a result of the settlers' efforts, the crea

label: Jamel
attackSummary: head(16p/2.9s); left hoof(6p/2s); right hoof(6p/2s); Bite(12p/2s)
description: Jamel were a slow moving reptomammal creature native to the planet Utapau. Jamels were one of the many creatures used as beasts of burden on their planet of origin and exported offworld for such purposes. Their natural resilience meant they made great livestock even in harsh environments.

label: jimvu
attackSummary: head(8p/2.9s); left hoof(6p/2s); right hoof(6p/2s); Bite(4p/2s)
description: The jimvu were native to the grasslands of the planet Naboo. The jimvu was an agile, six-legged, ungulate-like reptile whose best defense was its swiftness. Their main predators were the veermok and narglatch. They were exported as a prey species on various worlds where typically large predators where hunted for sport.

label: Jungle Rancor
attackSummary: left hand(30p/2s); right hand(30p/2s); teeth(40p/2s); left foot(20p/2s); right foot(20p/2s); head(30p/2s)
description: Jungle rancors were a colossal subspecies of the more common rancor that had evolved on the planet Felucia, but existed on other worlds through suspected "exotic egg sales" and poaching. This subspecies had extreme sexual dimorphism, with the males (referred to as "rancor bulls") being pale whitish grey, having 4 short facial-tusks used for display and an elongated tail for balance. The females we

label: kaadu
description: Kaadu were large, flightless reptavians that inhabited the swamps of the planets Naboo, Obredaan as well as the moon of Rori. They had sharp hearing and a keen sense of smell and adults of the species had distinct markings to distinguish gender. Kaadu were known to be fearless; consequently many were domesticated as steeds during times of conflict, or as patrol animals. This versatility made them

label: katarn
attackSummary: left claw(18p/1.5s); right claw(18p/1.5s); razorfangs(15p/2s); head(15p/2s)
description: A katarn was a predatory quadruped reptomammal native to the planet Kashyyyk. Katarns had slender bodies with rodent-like tails, and narrow faces leading back to a cartilaginous ridge protecting their neck and shoulders. Katarns were creatures of great importance in the Wookiees' culture. The Wookiees, who called the katarn the "Old Prince", hunted them in their hrrtayyk ceremony. They were a popu

label: kell dragon
attackSummary: front left claws(12p/2s); front right claws(12p/2s); teeth(20p/2s); spiked tail(15p/3s); head(10p/2s)
description: Kell dragons (also known as 'kell drakes') were were hardy, thick skinned creatures from the mountainous planet Rinderga. They were related to the much larger krayt dragons indigenous to Tatooine, but unlike their larger cousins were comfortable in both deserts and tundra. Kell dragons were believed to have been chemically altered by Sith Alchemy from the original krayt stock for use as effective

label: kinrath
description: Kinrath were a species of large, non-sentient arachnoids found on Dantooine, Kashyyyk, and several other planets. Kinrath had four legs and a leg-like, poisonous appendage coming out of their faces that they used to attack prey or other perceived enemies. All kinrath were blind but could sense heat which allowed them to navigate their way around and identify potential threats.

label: k'lor'slug
attackSummary: poisonous tail-stinger(12p/2.6s); Cut;Stab(12p/2.0s); Cut;Stab(12p/2.0s); circular teeth(14p/1.4s); head(6p/2s)
description: K'lor'slugs were poisonous vermiforms native to the swamps of planet Noe'ha'on, but could be found in sizable populations on other worlds (including Korriban and Taris). They were known to invade the darkest spots on unsanitary space vehicles and breed (aiding in their spread to new planets). Because of their notoriety as an aggressive and deadly species (especially among the spacers who encounter

label: kowakian monkey-lizard
attackSummary: left fist(4p/1.5s); right fist(4p/1.5s); Bite(5p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: Kowakian monkey-lizards were a bipedal reptillian primate species native to a jungle-like Outer Rim planet called Kowak. Their intelligence and cunning made them popular exports as exotic pets, with some specimens escaping and establishing wild colonies.

label: krayt dragon
attackSummary: front left leg(22p/2s); front right leg(22p/2s); teeth(30p/2s); Tail(30p/3s); head(15p/2s)
description: Krayt dragons are large, carnivorous reptiles from Tatooine, a desert planet in the galaxy's Outer Rim Territories. They come in two native subspecies and, despite their fierceness, are hunted for the valuable skulls.

label: kreetle
description: Kreetle were a fast breeding arthropod native to the planet Tatooine. They were was often found in cities, homes, and other urban areas and were universally considered a pest. They gave birth to young in the form of maggot-like larvae. Kreetles thrived on dead creatures, garbage and vegetable remains (including waste). They were found on many worlds having stowed away in supplies and once escaping

label: krykna
description: Krykna were predatory, non-sentient, spider-like creatures native to the planet Atollon. They were resistant to heat based damage and were highly tempramental, making them extremely difficult to tame.

label: kwazel maw
description: Kwazel Maw were giant aquatic slugs from the planet Rodia. They were a slow predatory creatures with remarkably tough hides that relied on ambush. Despite naturally inhabiting swamps, it appeared Kwazel Maw were equally comfortable on land. Their presence on other planets remains a mystery, although it is speculated that the eggs of these creatures may have been sold offworld as form of 'caviar' b

label: Kwi
attackSummary: left claws(8p/1.5s); right claws(8p/1.5s); teeth(24p/2s); tail(18p/2s); head(8p/2s)
description: The Kwi were large, bipedal saurians native to the planet Dathomir. They were herbivorous and yet remarkably sociable and intelligent. They were believed to be the degenerated descendants of the saurian 'Kwa' race. How they arrived on the various worlds they populated is unknown; perhaps they are the long descendants of the pan-galactic 'Kwa' or maybe they are just escaped circus specimens.

label: kybuck
attackSummary: left hoof(8p/2s); right hoof(8p/2s); Bite(8p/2s); head(20p/2.6s)
description: Kybucks were bipedal ungulates native to the planet Kashyyyk, and similar in appearance to the tauntauns of Hoth. These herding pack animals were fast and sociable, which made domestication and export offworld common.

label: lava flea
description: Lava fleas were large arthropods native to the planet Mustafar. As larval crystalline worms, lava fleas were able to feed on rocks. The lava flea would then continue digesting rocks and other nutrients, shedding its protective shell with time. Lava fleas were also very suitable mounts and exported as such to worlds with inhospital climates to other creatures.

label: leaf-tail
attackSummary: left claw(4p/2s); right claw(4p/2s); Bite(5p/2s); head(2p/2s)
description: Leaf-tails were a small rodent species native to the planet Dagobah. A non-sentient species of winged rodent, leaf-tails had membranous leaf-like tails that aided in balance and camouflage.

label: longtail gorg
description: Longtail Gorgs, were small tailed amphibians that could be found on several planets. This subspecies was slightly larger than the usual and had a tail (hence the name) and could lay unfertilized eggs. Their spread can be attributed to this variety being a favoured snack among the Hutt species.

label: loth-wolf
attackSummary: left claw(16p/1.5s); right claw(16p/1.5s); Bite(16p/2s); head(8p/2s)
description: Loth-wolves were a predatory canidae species from the planet Lothal with a strong historical connection to the "light side of the force". Due to their intelligence and ability to co-ordinate as a pack there is specualtion as to how "sentient" these creatures truly are. They were believed extinct by most xenobiologists, so how they got here is a mystery.

label: loth-cat
attackSummary: left claw(7p/1.5s); right claw(7p/1.5s); Bite(6p/2s); head(4p/2s)
